scope: WL57-WL66 (docs/worklogs/57_* .. 66_*) and experiments/fnto_rule57, fnto_reuse58, fnto_persist59, fnto_attr60, fnto_delta61, fnto_attr62, fnto_components63, fnto_direction64, fnto_clean65, fnto_rank66, with result JSON under results/fnto_rule57, fnto_reuse58, fnto_persist59, fnto_attr60, fnto_delta61, fnto_components63, fnto_direction64, fnto_clean65, fnto_rank66. Topic: learned intrinsic K (entry-to-first-exit operator of one homogeneous index-matched slab, sigma_t 1000 m^-1, RGB albedo .999/.99/.9, isotropic phase, 3840 ports of 2.5 mm, local dents <= 6 mm deep) as Rule-State (R) vs direct (D) operator, persistent state with same-checkpoint Full/Selective update (P), frozen-K attribution, ballistic/scattered tagging, directional-contrast objective, partial clean-label A/B, incoming-rank feasibility. All worklogs were read in full; model/geometry/training/runtime/evaluation/objective/label-override/tagging/estimator code was read and key numbers were re-read from result JSON. No coupled K-C solve exists anywhere in this scope; everything is K-only. Read-only; nothing was run except JSON printing.

implementation_facts.claim: The learned K is K x = B_G x + S_theta(G)[(1-beta_G) x] on a fixed interface of 3840 material ports (2.5 mm), 16 incoming and 64 outgoing bins, RGB flux in / flux out. The scattered part is 8 angular mixtures per channel: A = softmax(in_logits) of shape (8,16,3) over mixtures, O = softmax(out_logits) of shape (8,64,3) over outgoing bins. A and O are global parameters, independent of port position and of geometry; only the per-mixture spatial kernel depends on geometry.

implementation_facts.claim: Spatial kernel per mixture/channel = learned softplus(edge MLP) weights on 128 nearest receivers (kNN in REST coordinates, so the edge set is fixed across poses) multiplied by a FIXED hand-set prior exp(-dist/L)*0.0025^2/(dist^2+0.0025^2) with L = 0.0181/0.0058/0.0018 m (current distance), plus a dense rank-16 tail (U softmax over ports, V softplus). Columns are normalised and multiplied by a sigmoid survival mass, so each column is nonnegative with sum <= 1 by construction (no clamp, no damping).

The zero-collision term B and its column sum beta are computed, not learned: ray casting with q=256 fixed-seed (57501) samples per (cell, incoming bin), weight exp(-sigma_t * chord), binned to 64 outgoing bins, stored sparse. It is rebuilt in full on every non-rigid geometry change (no segment certificates).

Geometry input per port is 140 features: 16 local (rest xyz, current xyz, displacement, normal, area ratio, local thickness, normal spread, face id) plus 124 global values broadcast to every port (11x11 top-surface displacement grid + min/max/mean displacement). R encodes these to 32 channels with two message-passing blocks over 16 material neighbours plus a global pooled term; D gets raw features concatenated with fixed one-hop, two-hop and global means (560 channels) and no learned encoder.

Parameter counts: D 160,458, R 162,048 (the original D of 161,328 was replaced before any fit to match context scope), WL59 P 157,024. P is R with the encoder restricted to the 16 local features and the global pooled term deleted, so its state is dependency-local (two hops of 16 neighbours).

Training recipe (identical for D, R, P and every later arm): AdamW lr 0.003 cosine to 3e-5, weight decay 1e-5, grad clip 1, 6000 steps, final checkpoint. Each step uses ONE dent geometry (round-robin over 12 dents) plus rest and 2 fields drawn from 96, i.e. 12,000 field draws in total. Loss = 0.5*(rest + current) relative squared action error + 0.25 * delta term with denominator ||delta_target||^2 + 1e-4*||rest target||^2.

The training loss and the validation metric aggregate the 64 outgoing bins to 16 before comparing (at both the 1 cm and 2.5 mm spatial levels). The native 64-bin outgoing distribution is therefore supervised only through 16-bin sums. Validation scores absolute action only, never signed deformation or directional contrast.

Training labels are single-realisation (r0) actions of a sparse first-exit oracle operator traced with 2048 photons per input cell (125.8M photons per geometry). Evaluation references from WL57-A2 onward are a different estimator: importance-sampled per-field actions, two independent 64M-photon replicas per pose/field.

implementation_facts.claim: Light fields: 96 train / 32 validation / 64 test. The last 16 fields of every split are 8 equal-spatial, equal-flux pairs that are one-hot in incoming bin (bins aa and (aa+5)%16). Train and test generators differ by design: spatial widths 5/12.5/30 mm (train) vs 2.5/7.5/20 mm (test), angular kappa {0,2,8} vs {0,4,16,32}.

Acceptance contract used from WL57 to WL65 (1 cm cells, 16 outgoing bins): static coarse mean <= 0.10, coarse p90 <= 0.20, fine16 mean <= 0.15; signed deformation error <= 0.35 and correlation >= 0.90 on reference-qualified fields (SNR >= 3, first 16 fields); directional-pair contrast error <= 0.25 on qualified pairs (fields 48+2k vs 49+2k); F/S relative L1 <= 1e-5.

Selective update S recomputes encoder rows whose 16 local features changed, grows the changed set by one graph hop per message layer, recomputes raw edge values for edges touching changed nodes or with changed pair/prior features, and then ALWAYS redoes the global column normalisation and all derived coefficients. It refuses to run on a different rule object, changed weights, changed topology or changed material token.

WL58 implemented only an analytic float64 angular admission gate for a 64-in/256-out piecewise-constant interface on a GGX conductor probe. The persistent-state encoder/decoder, F/S updater, supervision and training of that candidate were never implemented.

implementation_facts.claim: WL60's outgoing-span floor projects (reference - computed B) onto the span of the frozen O aggregated to 16 bins, allowing arbitrary signed receiver values per cell; it ignores the incoming map, positivity, spatial coupling and geometry conditioning. It also checks whether the declared pairs collide under the frozen A.

WL63 zero-collision/collided labels come from one added assignment in the walker (zero-collision iff loop step == 1) and a sidecar accumulator fed the same exit events; an AST strip check asserts the original walker is restored, and per-packet gates compare tagged total to the untagged total and B+Scat to T.

WL64 arm B adds lambda * contrast term (lambda 1.4494, eta 0.00202 coarse / 0.0243 fine16) on one training pair per step (pair index (step//12)%8, fields 80-95) at the current and rest geometry. It supervises TOTAL response contrast against the original noisy r0 labels; arm A runs the same extra forward without gradient.

WL65 arm B replaces only train[80:96] (the 16 directional fields) on the 13 training geometries with the combined clean bank; train[0:80], validation and test tensors are asserted byte-identical between arms. 1,915 of 12,000 label draws (16.0 %) hit replaced fields.

WL66 analyses the model in its own budget-normalised incoming coordinates (scattered response = D_i A^T G_i). Because A is column-stochastic, the all-ones direction is always representable and the contrast space H*range(A^T) has dimension <= 7; the frozen basis is built with relative tolerance 1e-5 and a rank cap of 7. Floors are U-statistics over 8 replicas with a low-biased (eigenvalue tail) and a high-biased (held-out split subspace) estimator and a delete-one jackknife.

WL66 probes are localized one-hot sources: unit flux on one port in one incoming bin (2 geometries x 4 geometry-selected ports x 16 bins = 128 probes, 8 replicas x 32M photons each). Training fields are spatially broad (Gaussian widths >= 5 mm, sinusoid, checkerboard), so these probes lie outside the training light distribution.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL57: both fixed recipes (D and R) are NOT SUPPORTED; R is modestly better than D but no abstract Rule-State conclusion follows.
worklog_interpretations.source: worklog 57, A2/A3 Interpretation and Architecture Verdict
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Held-out absolute, delta and directional errors of 4 checkpoints against qualified references, and fair-cache lifecycle times. R has 36/96 directional failures vs 53-60/96 for D and equal cost within about 1 %. R bundles a learned nonlinear encoder, inductive bias and parameter allocation, so the difference cannot be credited to state separation.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL57: learned models learn part of the geometry response (delta error 0.2-0.66 vs 1.0 for the stale operator) although their absolute error is about 6x the stale operator's.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Delta relL2 on qualified groups and coarse absolute errors of learned vs stale-exact operators. The geometry-induced change (about 1 % of the action) is smaller than the learned approximation bias (6-7 %).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL58: the finite histogram interface is a representation admission failure independent of learned capacity.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Analytic optimal-projection loss and a triangle-inequality lower bound for two distinct inputs falling in one incoming bin, on a GGX conductor with alpha 0.04. It is a surface probe prospectively added to the candidate, not a measurement on the homogeneous volume regime.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL59: persistent state reuse is computationally correct and slightly cheaper, but a physically qualified saving is NOT SUPPORTED because F itself fails fidelity.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: F/S agreement about 1e-7, 66 % raw edges retained, 1.4-1.7 % time saved on the dent (28 % rigid), and the same blue-delta and directional failures in F and S.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL60: exclusion from the frozen outgoing span is not the dominant cause of the primary residual.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Only 2-4.4 % of squared error lies outside span(O) under a relaxation with arbitrary signed receiver values at 16 aggregated bins. It does not show the in-span response is attainable by the constrained model, and it did not bound the incoming side (done later in WL66).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL60: geometry-conditioned response generalises poorly (WEAKLY INDICATED) from the crossed replay (va1 delta error 0.62-0.95 vs tr11 0.17-0.23).
worklog_interpretations.source: worklog 60, crossed frozen replay and attribution table
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Frozen-model delta error against original noisy r0 labels with no SNR qualification, on 2 fields. WL61 then showed 89-94 % of that R/G gap was label error.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL61: historical evaluation-label error materially inflated the replay gap; no severe R/G geometry-generalisation gap is confirmed on that subset; a nonzero trained-geometry approximation error (0.13-0.17) exists.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Frozen predictions vs 768M-photon independent references on 2 train fields x 3 geometries; va1 blue unqualified. It does not test the primary pt0 population or training-label causation.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL63: the pair-7 directional failure is the learned collided response (wrong signed pattern and under-amplitude), not the computed ballistic term and not a cancellation.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Same-path tagged decomposition on one geometry and one field pair: 95.7-97.5 % of squared error is in the collided part. The upstream cause (angular mixing, spatial kernel, geometry conditioning, labels, optimisation, the (1-beta) interface) is not separated.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL64: a missing explicit directional-contrast term was not a sufficient correction; lower train risk with worse held-out risk is consistent with an objective-induced fit/generalisation trade-off.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One fixed lambda/eta, two seeds, contrast of TOTAL response supervised on 8 training pairs with noisy r0 labels: training-pair risk halves, held-out directional error rises 38-82 %. The trade-off explanation is not isolated from label-noise fitting, 8-pair coverage or weight choice.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL65: Monte Carlo precision of the 16 directional training fields is not a material limit on held-out directional fidelity; training-label noise in the replaced subset is an unlikely primary cause.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A/B with 16 of 96 fields replaced (16 % of draws, labels changed by 20 % relL2): held-out ratios 0.985-1.034. Fully clean supervision was not tested; noise of deformed labels for the other 80 fields is unmeasured; the delta gate passed mostly through the loss-scale floor (492/576 delta cells still SNR < 3).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL66: the shared rank-8 incoming interface itself imposes no material floor (rho <= 0.027 at 1 cm); the learned A does (0.37-0.55) but explains only 19-41 % of the model's probe contrast error.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Relaxed and frozen-basis projection floors on 128 localized probes at 4 ports and 2 geometries. The relaxed bound allows any coefficients (no positivity, no spatial structure), so it shows information sufficiency of rank 8, not attainability by the constrained family.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL66: the remaining roughly half of the probe contrast error is attributable to spatial coefficients, geometry conditioning, positivity/passivity structure and fitting.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Frozen A+O floor with free signed spatial coefficients = 29-52 % of model contrast-error energy. The complement is assigned by exclusion; none of the listed factors was varied, and the probes are outside the training light distribution.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL57/59/65: remaining candidate causes of the plateau are capacity, geometry conditioning, source-distribution coverage and optimisation.
worklog_interpretations.source: worklog 57 Interpretation; worklog 59 Interpretation; worklog 65 Unresolved Question
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing that separates them: no capacity, step-count, batch-size, light-population or geometry-feature ablation was run in WL57-66.

contradictions.between: WL59 primary directional result vs WL64/WL65 baseline arms on fresh source populations
contradictions.description: WL59 reports 5/24 and 4/24 failing directional cells (mean error 0.24) on the original test pairs. The same recipe retrained as arm A fails 15/24 and 13/24 on WL64's fresh pairs (mean 0.39) and 10/24 and 8/24 on the uninspected U65 pairs (mean 0.32), all on the same pt0 geometry. The original test population gives the most favourable directional picture; the worklogs report the numbers but do not restate the WL59 failure rate.

contradictions.between: WL57/WL59 verdict 'absolute-action norm thresholds SUPPORTED' vs the stale-operator control
contradictions.description: The learned models pass the 10 % / 15 % static norms with 6-7 % coarse error, while simply reusing the exact rest operator on the deformed geometry gives 0.5-1.2 %. In absolute terms every learned K in this scope is 5-6x worse than not updating at all; the static pass threshold is far looser than the size of the effect the architecture is meant to track.

contradictions.between: WL60 crossed-replay indication vs WL61 clean audit
contradictions.description: WL60 rated poor geometry generalisation as WEAKLY INDICATED from va1 delta errors of 0.62-0.95. WL61 measured 0.20/0.19 (R/G) against independent references on the same fields; 89-94 % of the gap was error in the old evaluation labels.

contradictions.between: WL60 outgoing-span conclusion vs WL66 frozen-basis floors
contradictions.description: WL60: only 2-4.4 % of the primary squared error lies outside the frozen outgoing span and a free rank-8 floor is <= 0.016, read as 'angular span not dominant'. WL66: the frozen incoming basis alone loses rho 0.37-0.55 of collided contrast, frozen A+O accounts for 29-52 % of model contrast error, and the frozen O floor is 0.28-0.36 at native 64 bins. Populations differ (broad fields with ballistic-dominated contrast vs localized collided probes) and WL60 never bounded the incoming side, so the statements are compatible but WL60's reading understated the angular-basis contribution to collided contrast.

contradictions.between: WL59/WL62 'directional pairs mostly pass' vs WL63/WL64/WL66 scattered-only measurements
contradictions.description: On total response 19-20 of 24 primary cells pass the 0.25 limit, but the computed ballistic term carries 0.91-0.99 of the pair-7 contrast norm, and the learned scattered contrast has error 0.91-1.12 of its own signal on pair 7, 0.95 on WL64 fresh pairs, 0.57-0.59 on U65 and 0.73-0.91 on WL66 probes. The total-response directional score is carried largely by the computed term; the learned part shows little directional skill wherever it was isolated.

contradictions.between: WL57 original Gate 1 vs A2 confirmation
contradictions.description: The same deformation family was 'not detectable' (0-3 of 16 fields per channel) with sparse-operator actions at 2048 photons per cell and clearly detectable (4-11 of 16) with importance-sampled 64M-photon actions on fresh dents. Data readiness depends on the estimator, not on the physics; the training labels were still the low-precision estimator.

contradictions.between: WL65 pair-7 result vs WL65 uninspected population
contradictions.description: With clean labels pair 7 gets 11-14 % worse and its Scat contrast correlation flips from +0.17/+0.21 to -0.24/-0.23, while U65 and WL64 populations change by <= 2 %. The worklog leaves this unexplained and excludes pair 7 from the decision rule as historically inspected.

contradictions.between: WL63 correction target vs WL64 intervention
contradictions.description: WL63 localises the error to the collided directional response, but WL64 supervised total-response contrast (dominated by the fixed computed B) with noisy labels, and WL65 used clean labels without a contrast term. A collided-only or clean-label contrast objective was never run, so 'explicit contrast supervision fails' is established only for the total-contrast, noisy-label form.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: In the homogeneous-slab volume regime the incoming-direction dependence of collided transport is low-dimensional (about 3-5 contrast directions) and small (0.7-1.0 % of response energy at 1 cm), so a shared rank-8 incoming interface is information-sufficient there; the evidence does not force a higher incoming rank for that regime.

open_confounds: Capacity vs geometry conditioning vs source-distribution coverage vs optimisation were never separated: no capacity, mixture-count, step-count, batch-size (2 fields per step, one dent per step), learning-rate or training-population ablation exists in WL57-66.
R vs D differ in learned nonlinear aggregation, inductive bias and parameter allocation at once; R's lower directional failure count (36 vs 53-60 of 96) cannot be assigned to state separation.
P (WL59) differs from R (WL57) by removing the 124 global geometry features and the global pooled term; the two were evaluated on different primary poses and never compared head to head.

Train and test light generators differ by design (spatial widths 5-30 mm vs 2.5-20 mm, kappa {0,2,8} vs {0,4,16,32}); held-out directional failures mix geometry generalisation with light-distribution shift.
Only 8 one-hot directional pairs exist in training (fields 80-95), each with bins aa and (aa+5)%16; coverage of the 120 possible bin pairs by the training set was not analysed against the failures.
Fully clean supervision is untested: 80 of 96 training fields keep single-realisation labels, and noise of deformed-geometry labels for those fields has no replicate.
A contrast objective on clean labels, or on the tagged collided component, was never run; WL64 used noisy total-response labels with one fixed lambda.

The (1-beta) remaining-budget split, the global column normalisation and the fixed hand-set distance prior (length scales 18.1/5.8/1.8 mm) all shape the learned scattered response; no counterfactual on any of them exists.
The cause of the blue (albedo 0.9) signed-deformation failure (0.38-0.42 in every arm and seed) was never attributed; WL63 tagged only one directional pair.

All references, including the 'independent' replicas, share one first-exit walker implementation; no independent-renderer check was made for the dented geometries (validation inherited from WL53-55), so systematic reference bias is not excluded.

WL66 probes are localized single-port one-hot sources outside the training light distribution and cover 4 ports and 2 geometries; the model error on them includes extrapolation, and the link to the broad-field pair-7 failure is not established.
WL66's relaxed bound ignores positivity, spatial structure and geometry conditioning; whether a well-aligned A is attainable by the constrained positive family is unknown.
WL66's non-evidence smoke run used the evidence seed formula and its per-channel category (B) was seen before the protocol commit; the worklog states no rule was changed afterwards.
The original primary test fields and pair 7 were inspected repeatedly across WL59-65; only U65 is uninspected, and it covers one geometry (pt0).
Two training seeds per arm; cross-seed residual cosine 0.96-0.998 indicates a systematic residual but shared labels, architecture, objective and geometry remain common to both.

The computed ballistic term has a resolved error of its own (9.3 % of its pair-7 contrast; 7.5 % coarse to 25.8 % native on WL66 probes) from fixed-seed q=256 quadrature; its effect on other pairs and on the learned remainder was not studied.
narrative_summary:
WL57-66 studied one learned intrinsic operator family on one fixture: the entry-to-first-exit response of a homogeneous index-matched slab with local dents, on 3840 ports with 16 incoming and 64 outgoing bins. The operator is a computed zero-collision term plus a learned scattered term. The scattered term has 8 angular mixtures with global, geometry-independent incoming and outgoing softmax bases, and a geometry-conditioned spatial kernel (128 nearest neighbours times a fixed distance prior, plus a rank-16 dense tail), normalised to be passive by construction. Geometry enters through a learned graph state (R, P) or raw summaries (D). About 160k parameters, 6000 steps, labels from a single low-photon oracle realisation.

WL57 compared R and D. Both passed absolute-action norms (6-7 % coarse error) and all algebraic checks, and both failed signed-deformation and directional-contrast gates. R was somewhat better, with no cost advantage (ratio 0.99-1.01). The exact stale rest operator has 0.5-1.2 % absolute error, so every learned model is several times worse than not updating. WL58 stopped before training: a 64/256-bin histogram interface cannot represent a sharp GGX lobe. WL59 ran real full and selective updates of one checkpoint: outputs agree to 1e-7 and 66 % of raw edges are retained, but the dent update saves only 1.4-1.7 % because geometry and ballistic rebuild dominate, and both policies share the blue-deformation (0.41) and directional failures.

WL60-63 attributed the failure with frozen checkpoints. Reference noise, F/S inconsistency and outgoing-span exclusion were ruled out as dominant. A suspected geometry-generalisation gap on a replay subset turned out to be mostly error in old evaluation labels (WL61). Path tagging on the worst directional pair put 96-97 % of the squared error in the learned collided response, whose contrast is weakly correlated or anti-correlated with physics although its absolute action is within 5-7 %.

Two interventions on the fixed family followed. An explicit total-contrast loss halved training-pair risk and raised held-out directional error by 38-82 % (WL64). Replacing the 16 directional training fields with qualified labels changed held-out error by at most a few percent (WL65); this covered 16 % of label draws, not fully clean supervision. Fresh source populations also showed higher baseline failure rates (8-15 of 24 cells) than the original test pairs (4-5 of 24).

WL66 measured incoming-rank feasibility on localized collided probes. Physics needs about 3-5 contrast directions, so a shared rank-8 interface could reach rho <= 0.027. The learned incoming basis loses 0.37-0.55, which is 19-41 % of the model's contrast-error energy; frozen incoming plus outgoing bases account for 29-52 %. The rest is unattributed.

Across the scope, what was shown is passivity by construction, computational F/S equivalence, rigid reuse, and adequacy of rank 8 in principle for this regime. What was not shown is any learned K meeting the deformation and directional contract, any quality-matched cost benefit, or any coupled result. Capacity, geometry conditioning, light coverage and optimisation were never separated.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL76: 'almost all of the native error (0.47) is the ring-lobe restriction'; the factorization 'moves the bottleneck from source transfer to post-collision angular expressivity'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A ring-projection residual of 0.45 of M, where M was formed with the q = 1024 SS and compared with a replica-only noise floor of 0.002. WL77A later showed the pure SS noise is 0.45-0.48 of the M norm and the noise-free ring floor is about 0.21-0.22 (two sources, non-evidence). The attribution is therefore confounded, by roughly a factor of two in the floor.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77: the remaining in-ring structure is 'azimuthal at order >= 3, or sharp features the low-order expansion cannot form'; the angular restriction is not relaxed by low-order azimuthal harmonics.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Projection floors 0.453 / 0.385 / 0.352 with a noisy SS inside M. With SS at q = 65536 the free-phase order <= 2 floor is 0.05 and extrapolates to 0.02; FIA-AZ / ring is about 0.30-0.40, under the frozen 0.5 gate. The recorded STOP stands as a historical fact; its reading is contradicted.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77A: 'A large part, plausibly most, of WL76's INSUFFICIENT FIT is produced by the deployable q = 1024 single-scatter quadrature noise'; the first-interaction factorisation is not what fails.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A synthetic prediction (reference - SS_true + SS_q1024) on three sources gives native 0.27, coarse contrast 0.51-1.24, against FIA's measured 0.32 and 0.69-0.75. No FIA was retrained with a low-noise SS, so the share that remains (ring restriction ~0.21, anchor snapping, capacity) is unmeasured.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77A: the W+UV boundary-far failure 'points to W+UV's absolute-position conditioning (an invariance and identity problem), not to missing capacity'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Energy invariants of one pair (s101 vs s50) equal within noise while A75 contrast is 0.131 vs 0.73. WL78 then showed the pair also involves a frame rotation / reflection, and that removing absolute position leaves the equivalent-context difference unchanged (ratio 1.00 / 1.03 native) while fixing interior transfer.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77A rejection of H1 CQR: its 'only mechanism-derived transfer is the orbit and translate identity, which any de-identified equivariant model, including a W+UV-Q control, shares'; out-of-orbit contexts rely on MLP interpolation 'from about 4 boundary configurations'; quotient / frame averaging is prior art; state 1.5-2.1 GB at the cap.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; design review with code spot-checks. No H1 prototype exists.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77A rejection of H2 RBG: projecting the first collision onto 2.5 mm hat functions (h > mfp) 'removes the incidence footprint shape it needs'; the near-diagonal resolvent block at unseen plane configurations is 'identified by smoothness only'; SS cubature aliased; pose-change cost exceeds the caps; covered by Neural Green's Functions / Element Learning / DeepRTE.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; design review.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL77A rejection of H3 LCR: 'Its transfer is carried by a published classical CPM / first-collision-source solve; the learned closure is likely vacuous (below seed spread)'; admissibility as a learned FNTO K is an untaken human decision; apply meets the cap only with an unbuilt kernel; no extension beyond g = 0, homogeneous, index-matched media.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; 'likely vacuous' is a prediction, not a measurement.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL78: absolute-position conditioning is a material cause of A75's failure in interior contexts; for boundary contexts removing identity is not sufficient, and the remaining failure 'fits a missing frame (orientation) equivariance of the operator plus late-training specialisation'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Measured: Q78 origin dependence 0, INT con_coarse 0.121 vs 0.319-0.545, no A75-style interior drift, BND_FAR 0.668 / 0.860 (seed-dependent). The interior part is measured on two seeds with a re-initialisation confound. The orientation-equivariance attribution of the boundary residual is inferred; WL79/80 never trained a model to test it.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL79: the frozen rank-16 G2 A/O 'cannot represent the exact symmetry images of the boundary training responses at the level it represents the originals'; exact angular equivariance needs an angular component that transforms with the frame.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Per-source oracle ratios 1.26-1.41x on BND coarse metrics, INT <= 1.07. The basis was fitted on the same sources in the original orientation, so in-sample vs out-of-sample is mixed in; whether this limit causes Q78's boundary transfer failure was not measured.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80: part of WL79's failure was orientation-biased fitting; the residual is 'consistent with a trade-off inside the global rank-16 factorisation (capacity / global sharing) rather than a pure optimisation failure'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Own-orientation gap fell from <= 1.41 to <= 1.15 with a 2-18 % regression of the original orientation; five marginal gate failures (1.258-1.266 vs 1.25; 0.101-0.103 vs 0.10). Only three restarts of a nonconvex problem; random restarts were worse in J.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80A Track A: BGC is 'not defensible as a mechanism for source generalisation' because of no identification (CE-1), wrong target (pair-conditioned angular factors act on a factor ranked below the spatial map), already-tested parts, and a structurally wrong normalisation (independent rho duplicates sum K, loose bound d instead of omega_c*d).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing new. The CE-1 argument cites historical seed disagreement (WL68 new-port contrast .94 / 1.22 / 1.36-1.44 at equal fit; WL78 BND_FAR 0.668 / 0.860).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80A Track B rejections: C4 NSM 'is a stored table of C1's columns, with no mechanism of its own' and its signed modal tail 'violates non-negativity by construction'; C3 CCA 'at rest is enumeration, and it degenerates to per-port tabulation on any other shape'; C2 SBG deferred as a conditional learned variant that 'moves the problem to chart and dent coverage'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; derivations and review.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80A: 'The only structural reason found for transfer to unseen sources is physical rather than learned' — in an isotropic, homogeneous, index-matched medium all source dependence enters through an exactly computable first flight, so transfer becomes discretisation convergence (C1). 'In this fixture, the learned-K question may be the wrong framing.'
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A derivation reproduced independently by both tracks and by WL77A. No accuracy or cost number exists for C1. The disposition states a C1 pass would not attribute the learned-family failures to learning rather than data volume, invariance, optimisation or the angular basis.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80B: 'C1 PHYSICAL BASELINE ONLY', qualified: not a method candidate; learning-free and ALREADY KNOWN (flat-source CP / first-collision source / MOC-style far field / successive orders); inadmissible as a learned K under FNTO v0.1; 'physical' means physics-based classical comparator, not reference, oracle or label source; the comparator role is unqualified (bias and cost unmeasured, not executable on the dent within the caps, no BASELINE_ROLES row) and a human decision. 'C1 ARCHITECTURALLY INADEQUATE' is recorded as the arguable alternative.
worklog_interpretations.source: docs/plans/wl80b/coordinator_disposition.md HIGH-1 and Final position; docs/worklogs/80B Architecture Verdict
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; a design review of an unimplemented operator. The label was chosen from four allowed labels and then qualified rather than replaced.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80C: the dominant limit of the R = 8 closure is its 'sufficient passivity bound' (sum lambda <= 1), not the basis family.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL81: 'The limit is basis-structural' — wi-independent weights plus Schlick-Fresnel reflection GGX lobes, whose albedo is non-decreasing towards grazing, cannot express an albedo that falls with incidence nor a refracted, coat-attenuated base lobe; 'A learned compiler cannot exceed its own direct-fit ceiling.'

The structural cause was not isolated by a basis intervention (e.g. wi-dependent weights were not tested).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL80D: after the sampler fix and one energy variant the fixed R = 8 closure 'does not demonstrate enough combined quality and validity under the frozen rules to justify learned-rule training'.

contradictions.between: WL76 post hoc reading vs WL77A coordinator check C1
contradictions.description: WL76 states the ring-lobe floor is 0.45 against a noise floor of 0.002 and attributes 'almost all' native error to it. WL77A shows the 0.002 noise estimate (replica half-split) could not see the q = 1024 SS quadrature noise that sits inside M; the pure SS noise is 0.45-0.48 of the M norm and the noise-free ring floor is ~0.21-0.22. Code confirms the mechanism (posthoc76.py and gate77.py both subtract the q = 1024 SS and estimate noise from reference replicas only).

contradictions.between: WL77 Stage 1 verdict / interpretation vs WL77A
contradictions.description: WL77 stopped because FIA-AZ / ring = 0.85 (> 0.5) and read the residual as order >= 3 azimuthal structure. With noise-free SS the ratio is ~0.30-0.40 (below the gate) and free-phase order <= 2 leaves ~0.02. The frozen STOP is preserved, but the gate outcome would plausibly have reversed; the reversal rests on two sources and an extrapolation, labelled non-evidence. No FIA-AZ training ever ran.

contradictions.between: WL77A specialist / coordinator record vs WL78 code audit
contradictions.description: WL77A lists the global 11x11 dent grid as an A75 source-location key. WL78's audit, confirmed in fnto_persist59/runtime.py (layers reads node[:, :16] only), shows the P network never reads it.

contradictions.between: WL77A check C3 reading vs WL78 mechanism result
contradictions.description: WL77A reads the s101 / s50 failure as an absolute-position identity problem. WL78 shows each such pair includes a bin-frame rotation or reflection and that removing absolute position does not reduce the equivalent-context difference on those pairs (Q78 / A75 native 1.00 / 1.03, contrast 0.91 / 0.93). Identity leakage is supported for interior sources only.

contradictions.between: WL75 interpretation (angular rank is not the bottleneck; the spatial map is) vs WL79 / WL80
contradictions.description: WL79 measures that the frozen global A/O loses 1.26-1.41x on exact symmetry images of boundary sources and WL80 leaves 1.15x after orbit balancing, so the angular basis is not neutral for boundary responses. The WL80A chair downgrades 'non-binding' to 'secondary'. The oracle gap (0.13 -> 0.18 con_coarse) remains much smaller than the learned BND_FAR error (0.67-0.95).

contradictions.between: WL79 verdict ANGULAR BASIS LIMIT vs WL80
contradictions.description: WL79's limit applied to the specific G2 basis, fitted in-sample on the original orientations. WL80 halves the gap by fitting on the orbit, so part of WL79's failure was orientation-biased fitting; the family still fails the frozen rule, but by margins of 1.258-1.266 vs 1.25 and 0.101-0.103 vs 0.10.

contradictions.between: WL80A chair record vs independent critic / coordinator disposition
contradictions.description: The chair designated C1 as 'selected primary' and wrote that a C1 pass would show past failures 'were failures of learning'; the lab summary also inverted the predeclared outcome rule. The disposition supersedes all three: no candidate is defensible as a primary learned-K answer, a pass shows only that the MC-defined K is computable from geometry on the scored strata, and a still-converging miss is affordability-limited while a plateau is a fail.

contradictions.between: WL80A lab summary vs WL73 / WL76 records
contradictions.description: The summary states every learned operator fits its 16 supervised sources and gives BND_FAR con_coarse 0.67-0.95. WL73 (all arms) and WL76 FIA were INSUFFICIENT FIT, and FIA's development BND_FAR was 0.96-0.99.

contradictions.between: WL80A disposition MEDIUM-7 vs WL78 cost record
contradictions.description: The disposition says A75's single-light apply (~1.34 ms) is amortised, not measured. results/fnto_srcid78/final/summary.json holds a measured A75 apply1 of 0.00207 s on the RTX 3080 Ti (10 repeats). Against that anchor the C1 estimate of 0.07-0.2 s is ~34-97x, not the 18-51x computed against FIA.

contradictions.between: WL80B verdict chair vs WL80B disposition
contradictions.description: The chair states 'the dented pose has no admissible W' and 'the far field has no feasible form' as facts. The disposition corrects both: the dent is unresolved for affordability / specification (a matrix-free ray-telescoped W meets every invariant and fails only on cost), and the falsification design's float64 Toeplitz far field contradicts the infeasibility statement.

contradictions.between: WL80C attribution of the Sample failure vs WL80D root cause
contradictions.description: WL80C attributes the defect to dr.select on width-1 opaque lobe parameters. WL80D shows dr.select is correct and the cause is `array == value` reducing to a Python bool in Dr.Jit 0.4.6. WL80C's C6 check compared two samplers sharing the same defect, so it was not an independent check.

contradictions.between: WL80C 'passive by construction' / WL80D 'PHYSICAL_CONTRACT control PASS' vs WL81 horizon finding
contradictions.description: The control's sum bound is a mathematical certificate, but the implemented runtime violated it above ~89.98 deg (single-lobe albedo up to ~2.6e3 at mu = 2e-7). WL80C/80D tests reached at most 88-89.95 deg or used a bounded VNDF integrand, so they did not see it. Those results were not re-evaluated.

contradictions.between: WL80C (energy bound is the dominant limiter) vs WL81 (energy constraint is not the binding factor)
contradictions.description: On 8 Disney materials removing the sum bound halves the error; on 300 coated-conductor materials the unbounded and sup-normalised arms are identical to three decimals (M > 1 for only 2.3 %) and all arms clear-fail. The limiter depends on the reference family.

contradictions.between: WL80D R3 failure vs WL81 post hoc
contradictions.description: WL80D records the candidate's highlight-width failure (|log w| 0.244) as a representation failure. WL81 post hoc shows R3 passes for every arm with 12,000 steps or a metric-matched objective (0.063-0.093), so width error is objective / optimisation dependent; the families differ.

contradictions.between: WL76 frozen Stage 1 rule vs continuation
contradictions.description: Stage 1 failed its frozen rule (1 of 108 checks, z^2 1.703 > 1.5). Part B proceeded under post hoc amendment 1 (user decision) replacing the failed check with a fresh-seed re-test. The physical validity of the factorisation therefore rests on a post hoc decision, as the worklog itself states.

contradictions.between: WL80C worklog reproducibility statement vs repository
contradictions.description: The worklog cites attribution scripts in experiments/fnto_compiled80c/diag/. That directory is empty and untracked; only the logs exist in results/fnto_compiled80c/smoke/.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A stochastic geometry-only term embedded in the deployed operator (here a q = 1024 per-cell single-scatter quadrature into 64 outgoing bins) must have its own noise measured against the signal before any fit or floor is interpreted; at q = 1024 it alone produces native error ~0.27 and coarse incoming contrast 0.51-1.24.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL77A checks C1-C2 (results/fnto_arch77a/coord_checks*.json), mechanism confirmed in fia76.quadrature / gate77.expr. Non-evidence, 2-3 sources.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Noise floors used in gates must cover every stochastic input of the statistic, not only reference replica noise.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL76 / WL77 floors used a replica half-split (0.002) that could not see SS noise of 0.45-0.48 of the M norm; the WL77 STOP was driven by it.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Raising the embedded quadrature to low noise is not free: FIA's rebuild is already 75 s (74.3 s quadrature) against 0.015 s for W+UV, and cost scales with q.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL76 cost table; WL77A C2 note (27-150x estimate is a specialist estimate, not measured).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The first-interaction factorisation with a source-independent post-collision response holds only for isotropic phase, homogeneous medium and index-matched boundary; it does not carry to anisotropic phase, surface / BSDF scattering, Fresnel boundaries or heterogeneous media.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL76 Stage 0 derivation; Stage 1 36/36 on that medium only (with post hoc amendment).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Learned inputs keyed on absolute position, material-axis orientation or face labels act as source-identity keys: they made A75's boundary predictions origin-sensitive by 10-23 % and can be removed at no supervised-fit cost (0.95-1.05x) and no apply cost (1.00x).
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL78 Stage 0 and Stage 3 / cost (results/fnto_srcid78/final/summary.json); verified in r57_geometry.py and q78.py.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Removing source identity is sufficient for interior transfer on this fixture (INT con_coarse 0.121 both seeds) but not for boundary-far sources (0.668 / 0.860 against a 0.25 gate); every boundary group still fails the absolute gates.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL78 Stage 4, two seeds, one fixture, re-initialisation confound.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A single global fixed angular basis fitted in one orientation is not orientation-closed for boundary responses (1.26-1.41x), and orbit-balanced fitting trades 2-18 % original-orientation accuracy for a residual 1.15x gap; exact frame equivariance would need an angular component that transforms with the bin frame.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL79 Stage 1 and WL80 Stage 2 oracles (per-source T, no learned model); marginal failures; three restarts.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Under the current first-triangle bin-frame convention exact angular symmetry labels exist only for the rest geometry; symmetry supervision or equivariance tests on deformed poses are not exact.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL79 Stage 0 geometry contract (normal error 0.073-0.079, non-bijective outgoing maps in the dent).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Linearity, positivity, passivity, rest-D4h equivariance and identity-freeness do not by themselves identify out-of-orbit boundary or deformed contexts; equal-fit runs disagree on held-out boundary sources.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL80A Track A CE-1 argument; empirical instances WL78 BND_FAR 0.668 / 0.860 and late drift 0.63 -> 0.86 after step 2k. The identification argument is a derivation, not a controlled measurement.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A learning-free explicit solver (H3 at theta = 0, C1 CP-K) is the only reviewed mechanism with structural unseen-source transfer, but it is inadmissible as the FNTO v0.1 learned K, its bias and cost are unmeasured, and its scope is g = 0, homogeneous, index-matched; any use (even as comparator) is a contract / human decision.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL77A coordinator decision (H3 grounds), WL80A disposition MEDIUM-3, WL80B disposition HIGH-1. Design-only.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A future learned-K claim on this fixture would need to state what is learned on top of the exactly computable first flight; the reviews found that candidates either learn what physics fixes (BGC), learn nothing (C1), or learn a compression that depends on the explicit operator as teacher (C2).
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL80A chair synthesis (final_architecture_decision.md §C). Design reasoning only; no measurement.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The source-independence of a learned function is necessary but not shown sufficient: FIA's source-independent, symmetry-invariant response still degraded on development BND_FAR (abs_coarse 0.39-0.42 vs ~0.13 on training sources).
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL80A chair disagreement 1 citing WL76; confounded by the SS noise and by FIA's insufficient fit.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A passivity normaliser computed as a supremum over a finite incidence grid is not an upper bound for Schlick-Fresnel GGX mixtures: the maximum sits at the grazing limit (argmax at mu = 0 for 100 % of WL81 materials). The supremum must include the closed hemisphere or be certified, and the runtime numerics must honour the certificate up to the horizon.

narrative_summary:
WL76 tested a first-interaction anchored operator (FIA): exact single scatter and second-collision mass from a fixed-seed Monte Carlo quadrature (q = 1024), plus a learned source-independent response restricted to ring-uniform outgoing lobes. The factorisation reproduced archived references in 36/36 packets on an isotropic, homogeneous, index-matched slab, but the frozen physical gate failed on one self-consistency check and continued under a post hoc amendment. The learned model did not fit its supervised sources (contrast 0.69 vs 0.27 for the rank-8 baseline) and cost 75 s per geometry rebuild. WL76 attributed this to a ring-lobe floor of 0.45; WL77 added low-order azimuthal harmonics, measured a floor of 0.385 and stopped before training.

WL77A's coordinator checks then showed both floors were dominated by the quadrature noise of the single-scatter term inside the diagnostic. I confirmed in code that both diagnostics subtract the q = 1024 term and estimate noise from reference replicas only. Noise-free extrapolations are about 0.21 (ring), 0.07 (FIA-AZ) and 0.02 (order ≤ 2), on two sources and labelled non-evidence. No FIA was ever retrained with a low-noise term.

WL77A rejected its three candidates (H1 canonical quotient kernel, H2 learned scalar resolvent, H3 learned closure plus collision-probability solve) on transfer mechanism, information or novelty. WL80A rejected BGC, C3 and C4, deferred C2, and designated the learning-free collision-probability operator C1 only as a candidate operator. WL80B labelled C1 "physical baseline only", qualified as: not a method, already known, inadmissible as a learned K under the FNTO contract, and with an unmeasured, undecided comparator role. None of these candidates was implemented.

WL78 removed absolute-position and orientation inputs from the rank-16 W+UV operator. Supervised fit and cost were unchanged, origin sensitivity went to zero and interior transfer improved to 0.12, but boundary-far transfer was seed-dependent (0.668 / 0.860) and inconclusive. WL79 found the frozen global angular basis represents exact symmetry images of boundary sources 1.26–1.41× worse; WL80's orbit-balanced refit reduced this to 1.15× with a 2–18 % regression and failed its gate marginally. Neither batch trained a model, so the link between this oracle gap and learned transfer is unmeasured.

The compiled closure work (WL80C, 80D, 81) established a corrected sampler, a horizon numerics defect that made the earlier runtime non-passive, and that a finite-grid passivity supremum misses the grazing limit. Direct fits passed the median but failed tail or width rules on eight Disney materials, and clearly failed on 300 coated-conductor materials under every energy parameterisation (best E_L1 0.129 vs 0.10). Runtime was at parity with a cheap analytic BSDF. No compiler was trained, and GPU, compression and rendering utility against an expensive reference were not reached before WL82.

scope: WL40, 41, 42, 44, 45, 46 (C:\Projects\ReST-GI\docs\worklogs\40_* .. 46_*) and the code in C:\Projects\ReST-GI\experiments\fnto_lego, fnto_lego_r1, fnto_lego_k44, fnto_diag45, fnto_dir46, checked against result JSON in C:\Projects\ReST-GI\results\fnto_lego, fnto_lego_r1, fnto_lego_k44, fnto_diag45, fnto_diag46. This is the first FNTO implementation: a four-term learned intrinsic kernel K (K_loc, K_glob, K_band, K_mid) per optical domain, composed with an explicit ray-cast free-space coupling C (no learned C). WL40 is a design-only review with no measurement. One scene (official Lego + red box), one rigid edit (box translation +0.44 m, T0 to T1), reference renderer Blender 3.5.1 Cycles. Read-only; nothing was run or changed.

implementation_facts.claim: K is a sum of four terms, b(x,w_o) = K_loc + K_glob + K_band + K_mid. Every network outputs coefficients from position / material / geometry / directions only and never sees radiance, so K is linear in the incident field. All coefficients are non-negative (sigmoid or softplus). Passivity is not built in (the module docstring says 'passivity is tested, not assumed').
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_model.py: module docstring lines 1-30; DomainKernel.bsdf_params, p_q, band_w, mid_w

implementation_facts.claim: K_loc is a per-point learned BSDF: rho(x)/pi + sum over 2 lobes of kappa_l(x) * GGX(alpha_l(x)), no Fresnel. rho = sigmoid (at most 1), kappa = softplus (unbounded above), alpha = 0.01 + 0.99*sigmoid. Inputs are a triplane feature (3 planes at 512^2 + 3 at 64^2, 8 channels each, 48-d) plus an 8-d material embedding. It is applied exactly to delta lights and, at camera pixels, to the port's 128 gathered directional samples.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_model.py: TriField, DomainKernel.__init__, bsdf_params, ggx, loc_response; experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_solve.py: render_pixels

implementation_facts.claim: K_glob is a global low-rank term per colour channel: sum_m p_m(x) * gamma_m with gamma_m = sum over ALL ports s of the domain of A_s q_m(s) E(s). Rank is 64 for the Lego domain and 8 for the box. p, q are softplus outputs of 2-layer MLPs (width 128) on the same feature. Entry is cosine-weighted irradiance, exit is isotropic, and there is no explicit distance or geometry argument.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_model.py: DomainKernel.p_q, make_kernels; experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_train.py: source_tables (gamma), make_kernels

implementation_facts.claim: K_band is a short-range directional term: sum over source slots s of A_s * sum over 19 hemispherical incident bins of W_b(x,s,w_o) * h_b(s). W is a softplus MLP (64-64) on a 16-d receiver projection, a 16-d source descriptor that is a linear map of the source MATERIAL embedding only, and 12 geometry numbers (offset/R_LOCAL, source tangent, source normal, w_o, all in the receiver frame). Bins: cap below 20 deg, 6 sectors 20-50 deg, 12 sectors 50-90 deg. Declared radius 5 cm.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_model.py: band_w, hemi_bin, DomainKernel.__init__ (src, W1x/W1s/W1g, W); experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_common.py: N_BINS_H=19, R_LOCAL=0.05, N_LOCAL=32

implementation_facts.claim: K_mid is a mid-range term: sum over coarse source slots c of A_c * Wm(x,c,w_o) * E_c, with E_c the area-mean cosine-weighted irradiance of a coarse cluster and Wm a softplus MLP with 9 geometry inputs (offset/R_MID, source normal, w_o). Declared radius 30 cm. It was added before declaration after synthetic contract B showed 70-140 % errors at 3-25 cm with band + global only.

implementation_facts.claim: Source support differs between Batch 6 and r1. Batch 6 used 32 nearest fine ports (band) and 64 nearest 4 cm coarse ports (mid). r1 uses 1.5 cm band aggregates and 8 cm mid aggregates over the full 5 cm / 30 cm balls, with 96 band and 128 mid representative slots carrying represented-area weights (amendment 1; a0 had 48 / 64).

implementation_facts.claim: The four terms are trained jointly against ONE target. The loss is L2 on log(1+radiance) of the summed prediction at camera pixels of isolated-domain first-event probe renders. There is no per-term target, no regulariser separating the terms, and their source supports are nested (K_glob all ports; K_mid within 30 cm including the first 5 cm; K_band within 5 cm). The three nonlocal terms therefore have overlapping targets; only the K-versus-C split is enforced, by how the probe images are rendered.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_train.py: predict, main (loss); experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_train.py: predict, main (loss)

implementation_facts.claim: Exit-direction supervision exists only at camera directions of camera-visible pixels. K_band and K_mid take w_o as an input but no training pair constrains them at other (port, direction) pairs. K_loc is trained only on delta lights (sun; in r1 also point and spot), never on a distributed incident field.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_train.py: predict (wo = px['cam']; lights from the light table); experiments/fnto_dir46/protocol/dir46.json: stage1_audit_before_design fact C

implementation_facts.claim: Training data. Batch 6: 1,400 train / 120 held-out probes, one sun per image with 0-10 shadow-only mask spheres, first-event masking that dropped glass internal reflection. r1: 1,000 train / 120 held-out probes in four families (sun x masks 25 %, spot 35 %, broad multi-point 25 %, multisun 15 %), 'intrinsic-all' masking (every non-camera ray arriving after a free-space segment is absorbed; Burley SSS and in-glass paths kept), no clamp, point-sampled, 512^2 at 512 spp. 24,000 Adam steps, 4 images x 16,384 pixels.

The passivity hinge (K_r1P, K_k44P; --passivity 1.0) adds mean(relu(albedo - 0.98)) over 32,768 sampled ports per domain and step. albedo = rho + sum kappa + glob + band + mid under a uniform unit-radiance field, and the band and mid weights are evaluated at w_o = the port NORMAL only. It bounds pi*L(normal)/E under one field, not the hemispherical exitance and not other exit directions.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_train.py: uniform_albedo_penalty (band_w / mid_w called with P.nrm[s] as wo), main (loss + a.passivity * pen)

implementation_facts.claim: C is a dense ray-cast relation table with no learned parameter (the learned coupling rule is declared empty). Each port casts 128 fixed cosine-distributed directions (Fibonacci disk, per-port rotation). Batch 6 starts 1 mm off a cluster centroid; r1 starts 0.1 mm off 4 on-surface samples. A hit maps to the port of the hit triangle's facing side; a miss is -1 (dark, no environment light); an inside face of a closed solid is -2 (no radiance). Same-domain hits (Lego to Lego) are ordinary entries. There is no transmission path through glass.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_relations.py: gather, map_hits; experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_common.py: K_GATHER=128, EPS; experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_relations.py docstring; r1_common.py: S_PORT=4, EPS1=1e-4

implementation_facts.claim: Incremental relation update after a rigid move: re-trace all rows of the moved domain plus every ray whose old segment touches the moved domain's old or new axis-aligned bounds (slab test, 1 mm margin); all other entries are reused.

Composition and iteration. State L[port, 128] is the incident radiance per gather ray. One Jacobi step: aggregate L into E_ind and 19-bin h per port; compute an isotropic sender value I per port = rho/pi*(E_sun+E_ind) + (sum kappa)/pi*E_ind + sum_m p_m*gamma_m + K_mid table at w_o = normal + K_band at w_o = normal; then L[p,k] = I[hit(p,k)] + per-ray exact sun-GGX lobe of the hit port. Start from L = 0. State is stored in fp16. No damping, clamping or relaxation.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_solve.py: State.aggregates, outgoing, step, Tables.band_sender, Tables.__init__ (Wm at self.nrm); experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_solve.py: State.outgoing_iso, gather_once

implementation_facts.claim: The sender folds indirect glossy reflection in isotropically with the unbounded softplus kappa as its albedo, and evaluates band / mid at the normal. Camera pixels instead use the full per-direction K_loc lobes on the gathered samples and band / mid at w_o = camera direction. The same K is therefore queried at different exit directions in its sender and receiver roles.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_solve.py: State.outgoing versus render_pixels; experiments/fnto_lego/fnto_solve.py docstring lines 12-20

implementation_facts.claim: Convergence and divergence rules. Batch 6: relative L1 change below 1e-3, at most 100 iterations, 'diverged' only if non-finite or (iteration > 5 and relative change > 1), so slow divergence was not flagged. r1: converged at relative L2 change below 1e-3; diverged when the median of the last 5 successive-residual ratios is at least 1 after iteration 8, or values are non-finite.

The spectral radius is a power iteration of the homogeneous map (sun off) from a random non-negative start: ratio of L2 norms of the fp16 state L per step, 40 iterations (30 in WL46), reported as the median of the last 10 (8) ratios. It is a norm-growth estimate on the gather-sample state, not an energy-weighted operator norm.

Evaluation arms: K_only (coupling off, compared only with first-event references), S_T0, D_stale (T0 relation table and T0 port sun fractions on T1 inputs), E_upd (incremental T1 table), E_relfull (full T1 rebuild). In every arm the pixel's own direct sun visibility is an input taken from the reference dataset's diffuse_direct AOV, including T1 visibility in D_stale.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_r1/r1_eval.py: prep (vis = diffuse_direct > 0), run (plan dict, render_pixels px['vis'])

implementation_facts.claim: The signed-change metric uses the luminance of LINEAR radiance differences (prediction T1 minus prediction T0 against reference T1 minus reference T0) on Lego pixels present in both views. 'slope' is a through-origin regression sum(d*d_ref)/sum(d_ref^2); the noise sigma is the MAD of the stationary pool.

The WL44 correction changes only the supervision's incident field: occluder hits closer than 0.3 mm are ignored for pixel visibility bits, port samples and held-out port sun fractions, and box point / spot light geometry is evaluated in world coordinates (four monkey-patched entry points of r1_train). Kernel family, loss, steps, hinge and the C relation tables are unchanged.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_lego_k44/k44_train.py docstring and Split2 / port_incident_off; docs/worklogs/44 sections C-D

implementation_facts.claim: The WL46 directional interface subclasses the r1 state. Sender nonlocal part (glob + band + mid) is read as 'n' (production, normal), 'basis' (per-port table at 19 bin centres: normal, 35 deg ring, 70 deg ring, looked up at the bin of the ray direction) or 'exact' (per-ray query). Sender K_loc incoming is 'E' (production collapse) or 'dir' (learned BSDF on the 128 gathered samples), with outgoing at the normal (R4) or along the ray (R5). Query directions below the hit port's horizon are projected into the upper hemisphere and counted (n_below). K44 parameters are untouched.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_dir46/dir46_solve.py: DirState.__init__, basis_table, ray_values, upper; experiments/fnto_dir46/dir46_core.py: nonlocal_out, local_out, bin_centres_local

implementation_facts.claim: In the WL46 glossy-plane scene the plane is an ANALYTIC control domain (rho 0, one GGX lobe, kappa 0.9, alpha 0.04), not a learned K. The 'dirread' conditions solve the Lego / box coupling with production semantics and use directional K44 values only for reads into the plane. Lobe importance sampling is 128 GGX-sampled rays per plane pixel.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_dir46/ms46_eval.py: module docstring, KAP / ALPHA constants, MSState

implementation_facts.claim: The WL46 one-step Lego diagnostic compares a ONE-bounce predicted indirect (first gather from L = 0) with the ALL-bounce reference indirect (full_r1 minus first_r1).

WL45's 'power K sends into C' is sum over Yellow ports of pi * I * area, with I the production normal-direction isotropic sender value from outgoing(0, h_sun), divided by the summed sun power on those ports (or on the whole Lego).

Each domain owns all of its parameters (Lego 6,531,047; box 202,335); nothing is shared between domains or with C. The edit is translation-only, so canonical and world frames coincide and rotation covariance is never exercised.

Reference-renderer semantics measured before training: Cycles Christensen-Burley SSS is object-scoped (crosses air gaps between disconnected parts of one object, not between objects), entry is material-agnostic, and SSS is not counted as a bounce.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: If a learned operator is applied recursively through a coupling (Jacobi / Neumann composition), the composed map must be contractive on the fields and exit directions the coupling actually queries. Linearity plus non-negative coefficients plus a first-event fit did not give this.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: Batch 6: 64/64 divergence, rho about 2.1 with K_glob and explosive with K_mid. r1 with corrected ports, support and 25x richer excitation: rho 10.47, 64/64 divergence. Convergence was obtained only with an explicit penalty (rho 0.68).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A scalar penalty on the normal-direction response to a uniform field is not a passivity guarantee for an operator whose output depends on exit direction; the bound holds only for the direction and field it was evaluated on.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: Hinge code evaluates band / mid at w_o = normal; the same frozen kernel read off-normal gives rho 9.4-17.1 and 46x flux on Yellow ports (WL46).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Every (location, exit direction) at which the composition reads the learned operator must be covered by supervision or by a structural bound. Outputs that are read but never supervised were the dominant source of composed error.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: Supervision only at camera directions of visible pixels; 64 % of Yellow area never observed, 82 % of predicted Yellow indirect from non-visible ports (WL45); directional reads at unsupervised directions diverge (WL46).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The incident field given to a supervised transport operator must be the one the reference renderer applied (visibility rule at near-coincident geometry, light geometry frame). constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL44 intervention: +1.56 dB Lego, box 16 -> 32 dB, -93 % leakage, from a 0.3 mm visibility rule and a frame fix alone.

open_confounds: Evidence breadth: one scene (Lego + red box), one edit (0.44 m translation, no rotation, no deformation), one sun family for held-out views, and one training seed for nearly every kernel (seed spread 0.10 dB measured on the baseline recipe only).

The reference's own energy behaviour for Yellow SSS was never measured inside WL41-46 (Burley conservation checked on a plane only). How much of the unconstrained kernel's rho 10.47 is extrapolation error and how much is faithful fitting of a non-passive camera-vertex reference was not separated in this scope.

The hinge and the rho estimate both use the normal-direction sender. 'Passive kernel' and 'sender read in a direction the hinge suppressed' cannot be told apart from WL42-45 evidence; the fidelity metric scores camera directions the hinge does not constrain.

The four K terms are trained jointly on one residual with nested supports and band + mid are stored together, so no failure can be assigned to a single term; rank versus support versus fit for Yellow is unseparated.

Capacity (width 128, triplane 512/64), operator family (2 GGX lobes, 19 bins, isotropic global exit), representative quadrature and optimisation (held-out monitor peaks at step 16k then drops 0.2-0.4 dB) were never varied; the 25-27.6 dB kernel-only ceiling has no causal decomposition.

Gate 2b (representative quadrature 0.27 / 0.20 versus 0.15) and Gate 2c (indirect field 0.24 outside the training span versus 0.10) failed and were carried. WL44's 'not a cause' tests used the frozen kernel at evaluation only; training with dense quadrature or fuller coverage was not tried.

Pixel-level direct sun visibility is an input from the reference dataset's AOV in every arm, including the stale arm. Total signed-change and A_changed metrics therefore mix an externally supplied direct change with the coupling update.

The static verdict compares FNTO (trained on isolated-domain probes, evaluated on clamped 'hist' references) with RNA (trained on full-scene T0 images in that regime). RNA was not evaluated in the unclamped r1 regime; the -9.08 dB gap mixes training signal, reference regime and representation.
The spectral-radius estimate is an L2 norm ratio on an fp16 state from one random start; K_r1P's late ratios alternate 0.66 / 0.70 (period-2 structure), and the reported value is a median.

C was never corrected for near-coincident geometry: 3.12 % of hits are closer than 0.3 mm and 4.95 % are 'enclosed'; the output effect on the composed image is unmeasured. The opaque gathered-field deficit (0.76-0.89) is not split between missing glass transmission, sender error and port-versus-pixel location.
Glass: C has no transmission path and glass indirect is 96-98 % missing; receiver response versus missing path is unresolved. Black's learned diffuse albedo is 0.27-0.30 of the renderer's.
WL45's interface attribution (B3b-B3g) rests on two views that behave very differently (Yellow indirect 2.51x versus 0.96x), and no per-port reference exists for ports no camera sees.

WL46's key K44 numbers (rho 9.36 / 17.1, 46x, 0.99x toward camera) come from single-view smokes; the full stage-1 audit, an exact-query glossy-plane run and a sampling-budget sweep were not run. The 12-28 % over-brightness of the best glossy result is unattributed within this scope.

The glossy-scene gain uses an analytic GGX plane, so it measures interface plus sampling, not a learned glossy operator. Directional reads lowered plane edit tracking relative to importance sampling alone (corr 0.95 -> 0.82, 0.93 -> 0.70, 0.68 -> 0.36) without explanation.
In WL46, ray directions below a hit port's horizon are projected upward (1.07 M such rays in the glossy scene's directional solve); its contribution to the divergence was not isolated.
Process caveats: WL45's B4 and first B2 / B3a ran on code not yet committed; WL42-46 carry post hoc amendments; Stage A probe target noise costs about 1 dB of the probe metric.
narrative_summary:
The first FNTO implementation represents each optical domain's intrinsic transport as a sum of four learned, linear, non-negative terms: a per-point BSDF (K_loc: diffuse plus two GGX lobes), a global rank-64 irradiance-to-isotropic term (K_glob), a short-range term over 19 incident-direction bins within 5 cm (K_band), and a mid-range irradiance term within 30 cm (K_mid). The code shows the four terms are fitted jointly to a single target, the camera-pixel radiance of isolated-domain first-event renders, with nested supports and no partition between the nonlocal terms. Only the K-versus-C split is enforced, through how the probes are rendered. C is an explicit ray-cast table (128 cosine gathers per port) with no learned part. Composition is a Jacobi iteration in which each port sends one isotropic value, with band and mid evaluated at the port normal, plus an exact sun-specular lobe.

Batch 6 diverged on 64 of 64 views. After six confirmed implementation defects were fixed (r1), the unconstrained kernel still gave a spectral radius of 10.47 and 64 of 64 divergences. A hinge on the normal-direction response to a uniform field gave 0.68 and full convergence at unchanged probe fidelity. Static fidelity was 24.49 dB against RNA's 33.57 dB. WL44 traced much of the non-Yellow kernel error to an inconsistent supervision field; correcting it gave +1.56 dB on the Lego and took the box from 16 to 32 dB. Yellow subsurface scattering then carried about 79 % of the kernel-only error, and the composed indirect light over-predicted Yellow by 1.74 times.

WL45 verified C on known fields (1.05 times, correlation 0.93) and located the Yellow indirect error at the K-to-C sender, mostly at ports never seen in training. WL46 showed a directional sender read is correct as an interface and, with lobe sampling, raises a glossy reflection region by 8.4 dB, but only as a hybrid with an analytic glossy plane. Read off-normal inside the solve, the frozen kernel gives spectral radii of 9.4 to 17.1 and diverges.

Several worklog interpretations were later revised. WL42's claim that the composition adds no error was wrong. Its signed-change headline (correlation 0.987) is dominated by the direct shadow change, which is an input; the coupling-updated indirect change has slope 0.40 to 0.55, and 0.17 on Yellow. WL45's "0.41 times sender" was a normal-direction artefact.

Specific to this four-term mechanism: jointly fitted overlapping nonlocal terms, exit directions supervised only toward cameras, a passivity penalty that binds one direction, an isotropic normal-direction sender, representative-sampled supports, and the cost of per-port directional tables. Stated more generally in the worklogs, but shown only on this mechanism and one scene: that a recursively composed learned operator must be energy-bounded where the coupling queries it, and that read-but-unsupervised outputs dominate composed error. The reference's own energy behaviour for Yellow was not measured in this scope.

implementation_facts.claim: K/C ownership contract (current): an optical domain is a connected material/medium region or a local surface interface, not an authoring object. K maps spatially and directionally varying boundary incidence to outgoing response at the FIRST EXIT into free space and owns local surface response, in-medium transport, internal scattering and transmission. C maps an outgoing boundary event through editable free space to the next boundary entry and includes exposed same-asset and same-domain exit/re-entry paths. Every path segment has exactly one owner; object identity must not freeze exposed interreflection into K; internal response must not be gated by direct-source visibility of the output point.

implementation_facts.claim: Coupled interface: i_a = e_a + sum_b C_ab(G_current) b_b ; b_a = K_a(G_intrinsic, material)[i_a]. Boundary fields keep material-coordinate position, incoming/outgoing direction and physical flux/radiance normalisation; mappings conserve area-weighted flux in current normal/tangent frames; near-contact spatial information must survive both sides. At fixed geometry/state K is linear, nonnegative and passive; scattered and ballistic contributions are distinct path families read out exactly once; repeated composition must be stable. The document states these are requirements, not properties of existing learned kernels.

Parameter/state ownership table: reusable rule parameters (source-independent, fixed across supported edits, no post-edit retraining); geometry-dependent intrinsic state (preserved only with a dependency/correspondence certificate); cached coefficients (invalidate with actual dependencies); free-space state (update for affected air paths); incident/outgoing radiance (recompute through the current coupled solve). Runtime inputs exclude target K, reference images, source-object identities, pose-specific oracle lookups and baked final radiance. The rule/state split inside K is explicitly a research hypothesis; no learned state representation or selective-update algorithm is adopted.

Research invariants as listed in AGENTS.md: learned transport RESPONSE not canonical baked radiance; SSS, transmission, local sharp scattering and exposed self-interreflection must have viable non-overlapping information paths; spatially varying incident illumination is operator input; parameter reuse and dynamic coupling are separate ownership contracts; no claim of non-rigid validity for a kernel whose internal geometry changed. Topic adds: direct and C-mediated illumination share the same source-independent K response; D_G (geometry-dirty) differs from D_T (transport-dirty); parameter preservation, output preservation and radiometric validity are separate properties; all four edit classes (rigid, local deformation, global bend/twist, self-contact) are mandatory long-term coverage.

implementation_facts.claim: Two different contracts are both called selective. (a) AGENTS.md user-confirmed definition (2026-10-13): recompute the COMPLETE owned learned state Theta_i of every transport unit U_i=(S_i,Theta_i) invalidated by an edit, keep still-valid units unchanged; never a parameter mask inside a jointly owned model; uses post-edit supervision. (b) Architecture section 6: F and S inside ReST-GI use identical rule parameters, inputs and fidelity requirements; F rebuilds all geometry-dependent state, S preserves certified-valid state and rebuilds every invalidated component; no retraining. Architecture section 7 says the two update semantics must not be combined silently and treats (a) as a separate reconstruction baseline.

GM programme (Roadmap table). GM0 local foundation: QUALIFIED for development (learned ER primary, learned E control; neither is a nonlocal K). GM1 (next): with frozen ER, sharp glossy/specular multi-bounce editable-visibility interreflection under a rigid occluder/object edit incl. stationary receivers; requires at T0/T1 (1) layered-BSDF physical PT reference, (2) full PT with the same frozen ER, (3) one explicit global mechanism, (4) stale/no-update and same-mechanism full rebuild, (5) directional/highlight, signed-change, multi-bounce, visibility-affected/unaffected evidence, (6) all update/solve/readout/memory costs with predeclared quality-matched edit-to-valid-output and per-frame accounting; no T1 supervision/oracle at runtime; an image match or a full retracer does not complete GM1. GM2: nonlocal material/interior response, transmission/SSS, heterogeneous multi-bounce without double counting (depends on interpretable GM1). GM3: state validity under local deformation, global bend/twist, self-contact (depends on GM1-GM2 mechanism). GM4: quality-matched lifecycle advantage incl. Neural Full Recompute when invalidated, Native Reuse when valid, separate PT re-render cost, prior-art novelty.

ER role as documented: frozen learned ER maps material descriptors to a compact reciprocal/passive LOCAL scattering closure with eval/sample/pdf; it is the local interaction inside an optical domain's response, NOT a spatially nonlocal operator, NOT a precomputed global interreflection field, NOT a replacement for the boundary-field interface, NOT final FNTO K. Selected 2026-11-10 by human decision as primary local-scattering development baseline; learned E kept as cheaper control. Modifying ER needs a new separately justified hypothesis.

ER closure as coded is a pointwise BRDF closure: f = sum_outer lam_r g_r + s(mu_i) s(mu_o) [lam_0/pi + eta^-2 sum_inner lam_r g_r(t(wi), t(wo))] with Lambert + 7 anisotropic GGX lobes (3 outer, 4 inner refracted), 5 attenuation knots per colour channel, one effective coat index; 64 raw parameters, 69 runtime floats per material; reciprocity exact by term symmetry; passivity through a softmax certificate (sum_r lam_rc <= 1); eval_closure, pdf_closure, sample_closure exist. It has no spatial argument.

implementation_facts.claim: ECRO v0 (the one GM1 mechanism executed, WL86) partitions paths by scattering-event count, not by K/C segment type: events 1-2 (q + Tq, T = S_ER C_G) are path-traced physically; the learned operator R_theta fills a 1270-patch x 64-bin x RGB table of radiance made of 2-5 scattering events at the second vertex (camera paths with 3-6 events); 'ECRO owns only paths with >= 3 scattering events'. The WL86 worklog text contains no occurrence of 'FNTO' or 'K/C'.

ECRO operator as coded: generator sees patch centroid/frame/area, 69-float frozen ER state, openness and the state-ray form-factor matrix (3 message-passing rounds), never radiance. Factors c, a, Q, P are softplus (>= 0). Application is linear in the source field s: u = c.s; one learned flight E1 gathered through the state rays (current visibility); plus a rank-24 global term P.(sum_j area_j Q_j u_j) that has no explicit visibility; B = a.(c.E1 + global). No passivity constraint is imposed. 735,664 parameters.

ECRO's 'selective update' re-traces only state rays whose segment crosses the old or new OBB of a moved box or that start on the moved box; the generator (model.factors) and the operator application are re-run in full after every edit. The STALE control uses the T0 state rays/patch tables with the current source field.
