open_confounds: Canonical documents are out of sync: AGENTS.md (2026-11-02) predates ER/GM/ECRO; Architecture and Topic (2026-11-10) predate WL85/86/86A; only the roadmap records them. Which text governs 'current candidate', 'active hypothesis' and 'selective recompute' is not stated in one place.

No canonical document says how a learned composed multi-flight operator (ECRO-type, ownership by event count, no coupled solve) relates to the K/C contract; it is neither declared compliant nor reported as a contract conflict.

No versioned successor to FNTO v0.1 exists although Architecture lists later requirements (reference semantics, ballistic readout, near-contact resolution, geometry-state invalidation) as not part of v0.1.

ECRO's F2 miss is small (0.003-0.012 above 0.06), in one region class of one held-out edit, two seeds; E2 differs from training in rotation and light; WL86A leaves training coverage vs operator-family capacity indeterminate.

E1 was inspected during development (look renders, dev oracle, dev-model renders) and E2 aggregate numbers at 128 spp were seen before the freeze (disclosed); only E2 radiance at evidence quality was unseen.

ECRO edit response is gated only in region D; region C change slopes 0.36-0.63 and panel LSPOT error 0.056 / 0.118 are stored but outside the gates, so 'edit-response gate passed' does not cover sharp receivers.

ECRO economics: comparator is a Python-traced Mitsuba/Dr.Jit path tracer with the same ER (WL84 found tracing is 85-95 % of wall in this harness); quality level g not reached; offline supervision (1,024 geometries x 4 lights) and training cost not amortised; one GPU; gate NOT TESTED.

ECRO supervision noise: training targets at 256 spp (~0.10 rel L1 per lighting); validation field error 0.078-0.079 vs target noise 0.054; 16-point source estimator. WL86A marks these as weakened but not excluded quantitatively for all cases.

ER is qualified on one coated-conductor family and 3 static images with a bias floor ~0.035-0.04; its local bias inside a multi-bounce room is controlled only through the REF-ER vs REF-P gap g, and mixed materials / nonlocal media are untested.
WL85's workload qualification is UNSUITABLE by one clause, so its mechanism-neutral characterisation is formally INDETERMINATE.
External Neural Full Recompute superiority is unmeasured on every workload; TransGI has no released code; RNA and 8DNA cannot run several fixtures natively.
The WL56 physical quality floor (blue +3.6 to +10.3 %) and the complete physical GI accuracy of even the exact oracle remain unattributed.
WL77A's finding that WL76/77 angular-failure attributions are confounded by q = 1024 single-scatter quadrature noise is unresolved; those verdicts stand unchanged.
Whether the passivity and near-contact constraints derived from recursive port-based K/C compositions transfer to other mechanism classes has not been tested.
WL84A's seven open human decisions and twelve unresolved reviewer disagreements are design-level and were not converted into canonical decisions.
narrative_summary:
The canonical contract separates intrinsic optical-domain transport K from editable free-space coupling C. K maps a spatially and directionally varying incident boundary field to the response at first exit into free space and owns local surface response, in-medium transport and transmission; C carries an outgoing boundary event through editable air to the next boundary entry, including same-asset and same-domain re-entry. Each path segment has one owner. K must be linear, nonnegative and passive at fixed geometry, source-independent, and expressed in material coordinates; ballistic and scattered light are read out once each. These are stated as requirements, not achieved properties. The WL53 result JSON confirms the ownership rule's empirical basis (disjoint rho 0.42-0.82, duplicated ownership 4.75).

Two things are called selective. AGENTS.md defines selective recomputation as retraining the complete learned state of invalidated Surface-Owned units. Architecture defines F/S as same-rule state rebuilds with no retraining and treats the Surface-Owned contract as a separate baseline.

The current programme is GM0-GM4. GM0 is closed: the learned ER closure is the primary local-scattering baseline. In code it is a pointwise reciprocal, certificate-passive BRDF closure with 69 runtime floats and no spatial argument; the documents say explicitly that it is not a nonlocal K. GM1 asks for sharp glossy multi-bounce interreflection under a rigid edit with frozen ER, three reference levels, stale and full-rebuild controls and complete cost accounting. GM2-GM4 are directional commitments only.

One GM1 mechanism has been run. ECRO v0 path-traces events 1-2 and fills a 1270-patch by 64-bin table of higher-order radiance with a linear, non-negative, geometry-conditioned operator. Its result JSON confirms the roadmap: stationary error 0.003-0.006, one region class on the held-out edit at 0.063 / 0.072 against 0.06, verdict NOT SUPPORTED under frozen gates, economics not gated (descriptive 3-6x against a Python-traced comparator). ECRO partitions by event count rather than K/C segment and uses no coupled solve; no canonical document places it relative to the K/C contract.

Baseline terminology is binding: Neural Full Recompute, Native Reuse, internal F/S and path-traced re-render are four separate roles. The WL69 protocol mislabel is confirmed in its JSON. External neural-rebuild superiority is unmeasured everywhere.

Undecided items are numerous: the GM1 mechanism, the ER-to-global boundary, learned K adequacy, persistent within-K reuse, the physical quality floor, non-rigid coverage, and a successor to FNTO v0.1. No document grants authorisation for any batch.

The documents disagree in currency. AGENTS.md stops at 2026-11-02, still names FNTO v0.1 and K_k44P as current, cites sections that no longer exist, and does not mention ER or GM. Architecture and Topic predate WL85/86 and say global transport with ER is untested; the roadmap records that it was tested once. The roadmap's statement that edit-response gates passed covers only broad region D; sharp-receiver change slopes of 0.36-0.63 are stored but ungated.

scope: WL67-WL75 incl. 71A, 71B, 72A, 74A (docs/worklogs/67_* .. 75_*); code in experiments/{baseline_sup67, fnto_repr68, xbench69, sunreuse70, fnto_cover71, fnto_drift71a, fnto_attrib71b, fnto_cmp72, fnto_src73, fnto_ato74, fnto_rank75} (+ fnto_rule57/r57_geometry.py for the shared geometry features, fnto_walker71c for WL72A); result JSON/CSV under results/ of the same names. Read-only; all 13 worklogs read in full; key numbers spot-checked against results JSON/CSV and key mechanisms against code. Fixture regime throughout WL68-75: one homogeneous isotropic index-matched 10x10x1 cm medium slab family (sigma_t 1000 /m, albedo 0.999/0.99/0.9), 3,840 ports at 2.5 mm, 16 incoming / 64 outgoing bins, 1 cm coarse cells (240).

implementation_facts.claim: The learned intrinsic K (WL59 P family, used WL68-75) is K[i,j,a,o,c] = d[i,a] * sum_r A[r,a,c] T[i,j,r,c] O[r,o,c] with A = softmax over mixtures (global), O = softmax over 64 outgoing bins (global), d = 1 - beta (geometry-only quadrature). T has no incoming-bin index. Rank M = 8 mixtures, TR = 16.

Spatial map T = T_W + T_UV: W = softplus(edge MLP) * prior on the 128 nearest rest-coordinate neighbour edges of the source; U = softmax over ALL destination ports (rank 16 per mixture/channel); V = softplus(node head of source); mass = sigmoid(node head); scale = mass/(sum W + sum V) so T >= 0 and sum_j T = mass < 1 (passivity by construction).

The network's per-port input features contain absolute rest position and absolute current position: local = [xyz0/.05, xyz/.05, displacement/.006, normal, area ratio, thickness, normal spread, face id] (+124 broadcast global features). At rest all top-face ports share identical non-position features, so sources are distinguishable only by position (the WL71 Stage-1 statement).

Fitting objective J = mean over (source, channel) of [ (rel sq err native + fine16 + coarse)/3 + rel sq err of the centred (H = I - 1/16) coarse response divided by d (the 'contrast' term) ]. Contrast is weighted equally with the mean of the three absolute terms.

Reported metrics are rho = sqrt(sum error / sum signal) pooled per group, with jackknife 95 % bounds over reference replicas; worklogs quote the upper bound of the worst RGB channel. The interval therefore reflects reference Monte Carlo noise only (bounds are typically +-1e-4), not model-seed variance.

Parameter group 'net' trains every parameter except in_logits/out_logits (A/O frozen); 'all' trains everything. WL71-73 'P_' inits load the WL59 checkpoint and overwrite A/O with the WL68 net_all_5902 angular bases.

WL72 Candidate A's symmetry term compares angle-integrated responses only (sum over incoming a and outgoing o), permuted over ports by exact D4 (x z-flip at rest) symmetries; loss = J + lambda*L_sym with relative squared error. It carries no constraint on angular equivariance (A/O frozen).

WL72 Candidate B (RSK) uses no absolute position: per-port descriptor = normal, thickness, edge distance, area ratio, normal spread, displacement; relations to 128 neighbours and 240 coarse-cell centroids are expressed in the source's local frame; T = mass*(w_loc + w_far*area share)/(sum), mass = sigmoid. Three MLPs (phi_loc, phi_far, phi_m).

WL74 oracle arms use the same operator with rank-generic code; A = softmax(dim 0), O = softmax(dim 1), per-source T projected onto the capped simplex {T>=0, sum<=1}; per-source T is a latent fitted variable (not a learned rule). G2 (rank 16) nests G0 by duplication.
WL75 rank-16 model is initialised by duplicating rank-8 mixture r mod 8 of P_590x in the rank-dependent final layers; A/O are the frozen G2_r0 logits.
WL71A arms: R trains loss J, N trains J/J0 (J0 computed once at init); 'net' group, checkpoints saved at fixed steps; Adam + clip_grad_norm 1.0, torch.manual_seed(0).

WL71B counterfactual is a full 2^4 factorial over (W_raw, U, V_raw, mass) swapped between Early (2,000 steps) and Late (20,000 steps) checkpoints, with scale recomputed by the original algebra; hybrids are diagnostic, not reachable networks.

WL69 8DNA arm (D8): one trained slab asset (final.ckpt), rendered with neuralvolpath max_depth 10 / rr_depth 5; T1 is produced by translating the asset instance (to_world) with NO retraining. It is therefore a Native Reuse arm, not a neural rebuild.

WL69 quality matching rule: QM = lowest spp at which both Cycles realizations have M1 >= arm and M2, M3, M4 <= arm (arm value = worst over T0/T1); QM_contract = lowest spp with all ruled groups passing in both realizations. ReST-GI prediction is read as nee + ball (amendment 2 fix).

WL70 reuse validation checks rest-mesh hash (D1), medium tuple (D2), Kabsch rigid residual <= tol (D3), material-frame light list (D4), material-frame camera directions (D5) and replays every cached source sample through the current full-scene shadow test requiring a bit-identical visibility mask (D6). D7 (estimator identity) is stored in the cache but the check is hard-coded: rep['checks']['D7_estimator'] = True.

WL67 W2 neural timings (RNA rebuild 11,648 s, 8DNA schedule 6,354 s, inference 6.8 s / 100.7 s) are constants inherited from WL27 on an RTX 5080, not re-measured; the neural quality numbers are stored WL22 outputs re-scored (reproduction diff 0.0 / 6e-8). PT timing was measured on LabServer69's RTX 3090.

WL73 S16-R keeps 16 sources, removes 4 flat-interior rest-symmetry duplicates (slots 6, 8, 9, 12) and adds 4 boundary-context sources (TBE port 3439, TBC 3823, SM 408, SR 527) by geometry-only rules; removal and addition are a single coupled intervention.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL67: ReST-GI has a quality-matched advantage on no executed workload; W1 cannot support a cost claim because path tracing the small fixture is cheaper than its oracle K.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One small two-slab fixture, four fixed views: Cycles 4 spp 4.67 s (12/12) vs oracle S 189.8 s (9/12). Scene scale, view count and update frequency were not varied; the compared ReST-GI arm is an exact oracle, not a learned K (the learned WL59 K was ineligible and never composed).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL67: the oracle's per-port signed-change precision (M4) exceeds single-realization Cycles up to 1024 spp; Cycles would need ~3,000-6,000 spp to match.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: M4 S 0.077/0.032/0.047 vs Cycles-1024 0.122/0.055/0.091 is measured; the 3,000-6,000 spp figure is a labelled 1/sqrt(spp) extrapolation, and the metric is partly limited by reference noise.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL67: external neural baselines (RNA, 8DNA) are dominated by quality-matched path tracing on the teaset.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: ROI display MAE of stored WL22 frozen/refit outputs (0.103-0.124) vs fresh Mitsuba PT 64 spp (0.076-0.077, 0.52 s). Quality is physically aligned; timing is cross-machine (neural from RTX 5080).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL69: most of 8DNA's 15-20 % deficit is attributable to the learned asset, not the renderer.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Mitsuba volpath under 8DNA's unit convention passes 12/12 (max 0.85 %) while 8DNA fails; render depth (max_depth 10, depth 64 crashes) and the 30-epoch training budget were not varied.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL69/WL70: ReST-GI is dominated by / narrowly beats 'quality-matched Full Recompute'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: CAK update time (24.0 s; 2.09 s with sun reuse) vs Cycles path-traced re-render time at 16 spp (2.3-2.4 s manifest; 2.05-2.09 s Blender-internal). Under the project's binding terminology this is a path-tracing re-render comparison; no neural rebuild was timed, and the 8DNA arm is Native Reuse.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL70: the material-frame first-order sun state is reusable across the C1 rigid edit; rigid motion alone does not guarantee it.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Physical identity vs independent replicas (group differences <= 0.27 %, R within limits), 0/16 M visibility mismatches, and four rejected controls (sun angle, occluder, albedo, 90-degree rotation). Scope: one translation, one collimated sun, unoccluded.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL68: the WL59 shortfall on the fit probes is on the angular side of its learned parameters; the generalisation failure is located in the geometry-to-spatial-coefficient map at unseen sources, not in the angular bases, optimizer or passivity.

No same-family cross-source teacher was run in WL68, so identifiability vs capacity was not separated there.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL71: expanded source coverage supports an identifiability explanation for part of the WL68 failure; number/spread of sources, not label precision, matters; generalisation is supervision-local.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A cost claim cannot be established on these small fixtures by per-view rendering comparisons alone; scaling with scene size, view count and update frequency has not been measured in either direction.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Comparisons against external neural methods must separate Neural Full Recompute, Native Reuse and path-traced re-render; a native-reuse baseline that fails the physical contract statically (8DNA 3-7/12) is ineligible for superiority claims, and Neural Full Recompute superiority is unmeasured.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Reusing cached transport state after an edit requires an explicit dependency contract with material-frame light/camera directions and source visibility; rigidity of the motion is not sufficient (a 90-degree rotation in the same world volume and an occluder both invalidate the state).
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL70 invalidation controls N2, N4; sr70_state.validate

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Fit-population accuracy and accuracy at trained positions under a changed geometry say nothing about transfer: evaluation needs independent source positions away from supervised sources and their exact symmetry images, and a signed-change test with qualified signal inside the deformation footprint.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL68 (fit .039/.087/.133 vs new ports .56/.61/.94; H2 pass with change corr ~0); WL72 dev vs confirmation; WL72 CONFDEF unmeasured (3/8)

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A geometry->T map conditioned on absolute position and supervised at 4-16 sources converges to position-specific solutions; transfer is limited to roughly 5-18 mm from a supervised source on the same face and fails at corners, side faces and unsupported edge contexts.

open_confounds: Scale: all cost comparisons use one small fixture each (two-slab W1; 10x10x1 cm slab over a floor C1), 3-4 fixed views, one machine; costs vs scene size, view count and update frequency were never varied.

Timing definitions differ by arm: Cycles times exclude Blender start-up and scene construction (WL69 manifest includes Python readback, Blender-internal does not); CAK times exclude resident K load (4.1 s), the offline oracle K (~380 s per configuration, 2.04 GB) and in WL70 the 21.5-21.7 s T0 cache construction. The WL70 13 % margin flips with the timing definition.

The ReST-GI arms in WL67/69/70 are exact oracles (2.5 mm oracle K, CAK aggregation), not learned K; the learned WL59 K has never been run in a coupled solve, so no learned-method cost or quality point exists against a path tracer.
WL67 W2 timing is cross-machine (neural RTX 5080 inherited, PT RTX 3090) and the neural arms are stored outputs; 8DNA could not be re-executed on LabServer69 in WL67.

8DNA's 15-20 % static deficit in WL69 was not attributed: render depth (max_depth 10; depth 64 crashes in released code), 30-epoch schedule, asset capacity and null-boundary sampling were not varied; 6-9 of 96 renders crashed.
M4 (per-port signed change) on W1 is partly reference-limited; how much of the oracle's M4 advantage is noise cancellation is unresolved.

Reported 'upper 95 %' bounds are jackknife intervals over reference replicas only; model variance is represented by 2 seeds per arm, and the fitting code is not run-to-run deterministic (J trajectories differ 2-5 %). Three WL68 all-group fits with near-identical fit scores differ at new ports by contrast .94 vs 1.22 vs 1.36-1.44.

Final-iterate protocol vs training drift: every reported transfer number is a 20,000-step final iterate while 2,000-step checkpoints transfer better; the cause of the drift (low-gradient Adam phase, unconstrained directions, target-noise fitting) is unattributed, and it was observed from pretrained P_590x inits (one init per arm in WL71A).

Boundary context is confounded with coarse-grid sub-position: 1 cm cells are aligned with slab edges, and the WL73 boundary sources sit at cell-corner sub-cells. Metrics, targets and the contrast term are all defined on this grid.
Rank 16 (WL75) doubles both angular atoms and the spatial W/U/V state; angular and spatial capacity are not separated. A vs B (WL72/73) also differ in parameter count (157,024 vs 31,656).
The S16-R intervention couples adding 4 boundary sources with removing 4 interior sources; one S16 layout and one S16-R layout only; coverage-density scaling is known at two levels (4, 16).
Deformation evidence is weak: training geometries are rest + pt0 only; WL72 confirmation deformation unmeasured; WL73 te0 and WL75 cf1 are near-training-pose checks (cf1 4.4 mm from the pt0 centre).

d = 1 - beta comes from a fixed-seed q=256 Monte Carlo quadrature that differs from a fresh build by rel L2 ~0.10 and is not exactly symmetric under slab symmetries (WL75: 73/240 pairs pass); its effect on the oracle floors and on the 'exact' symmetry loss was estimated only by non-evidence proxies (WL74A: ~+0.004 con pooled).

The fixed A/O used in WL71-73 are the WL68 net_all_5902 bases, themselves fitted on 4 sources; the rank-8 shared optimum is not certified (WL74 restart spread 120 %), and all oracle values are achieved optimisation results, not lower bounds.

Oracle T is a per-source latent fitted on a replica of the same source: it shows that admissible coefficients exist, not that any geometry-conditioned rule can produce them. Existence of a smooth source-independent family member that meets the criteria is undecided (WL71 Unresolved 1).

WL75 Stage 3 references were generated on a different machine (local RTX 5080, torch 2.8) than the training references and controls (LabServer63, torch 2.3.1); provenance of scores agrees to 3e-6 but the cross-machine reference set is labelled, not tested. INT4's interior gain rests on 8 sources, 6 within 2.5-3.5 mm of training-source images.

Regime: homogeneous isotropic (g = 0) index-matched medium, collided first-exit transport with ballistic part separated; nothing in WL68-75 concerns surfaces, glossy transport, heterogeneous media or the coupled K/C solve.
WL74A evidence is agent-written CPU Monte Carlo and relaxations (non-evidence, rest geometry, point estimates, scratch scripts partly overwritten) and was produced after WL74 was committed.
narrative_summary:
WL67-70 measured cost against path tracing on two small fixtures. On the WL56 two-slab medium, Cycles re-render met the 3 % contract at 4 spp in 4.67 s, while the exact-domain oracle selective update took 189.8 s and failed it (9/12, blue bias 10.4 %). The oracle won only on per-port signed-change precision (slower, partly reference-limited) and on a 0.69 s rigid resident update that fails the contract. On the teaset, 64-spp Mitsuba (0.52 s) beat frozen and refitted RNA/8DNA, with neural timings inherited from another machine. On the WL55 floor fixture, CAK passed 12/12 where frozen-asset 8DNA failed (3-7/12), but Cycles matched CAK at 16 spp in 2.3-2.4 s against a 24.0 s update. Validated sun-state reuse cut that to 2.09 s: 13 % ahead by manifest timing, a tie by Blender-internal timing, and behind Cycles at the bare contract (1.2 s). All ReST-GI arms were oracles, not learned K, and no neural rebuild was timed.

WL68-75 tested the learned intrinsic K (global angular bases A/O, geometry-conditioned spatial factor T) on one slab family. With all parameters free it fits its supervised sources (.039/.087/.133), but fails at new sources (.56/.61/.94). The frozen WL59 bases have an admissible contrast floor of .74-.76. The WL68 bases pass as an oracle at interior sources (.15-.21) but sit at 0.24-0.27 at boundary and coarse-cell-corner sources. A refitted rank-8 basis reached 0.22 with interior regressions, and rank 16 reached 0.13-0.17; these are achieved values, not bounds.

Sixteen sources instead of four halved held-out error, with equal-photon and 4x-photon arms equal, but transfer stayed local: good within about 5-18 mm of a supervised source, failing at corners, side faces and unsupported edges. A symmetry loss and a position-free relational kernel improved development ports but not independent confirmation ports. Adding boundary sources helped at 5 mm, not at 16-33 mm, and degraded accuracy near removed sources. A rank-16 learned K reached its oracle at supervised sources (0.270 to 0.131) and improved interior sources, but left independent far-boundary contrast unchanged (0.79 to 0.80-0.82, against oracles of 0.265 and 0.159) at 1.85x apply cost. Signed deformation failed for every learned map.

Fine-tuning drift is a separate measured effect: unseen-source error is lowest at 500-2,000 steps and about five times worse by 20,000 while fit error keeps improving. A factorial attribution found several redundant components, none recovering more than 24 % alone. All verdicts use final iterates.

Formal verdicts were: WL67 no advantage, WL68 B, WL69 B, WL70 A (fragile), WL71 B, WL72 INCONCLUSIVE, WL73 INSUFFICIENT FIT, WL74 C+D, WL75 no independent generalisation benefit.

Checks against code and result JSON matched the worklogs, with two discrepancies: WL70's estimator-identity check (D7) is hard-coded true, and WL67 quotes one signed-change figure from the better realization. The main unresolved confounds are fixture scale, timing definitions, the coupling of boundary context with the 1 cm metric grid, drift under the final-iterate rule, and two seeds per arm.

implementation_facts.claim: WL47 synthetic domain: 4 strip ports x 12 angular bins (3 rings 0-30-60-90 deg x 4 azimuth sectors, projected solid angles sum to pi) = 48 boundary states. S0 = Lambertian entry (t 0.9), port-to-port exp(-|dx|/2) redistribution (max column albedo 0.7), Lambertian exit, built as G x E-map (rank 4). S1 = internal mirror at depth 1: a beam entering port p in bin j exits at x_p - 2h tan(theta) cos(phi), in the mirrored-azimuth bin (0.7) and its two neighbours (0.1 each), reflectance 0.8 (rank 40).

WL47 equal-irradiance pairs: for every port with E>0 the partner field redraws a new 1-3 bin angular distribution with exactly the same per-port E. The Stage C test set is 64 configurations = 32 random + 16 pairs (A and B members); train/test separation is asserted by byte comparison.

WL47 'learned operators' A0/A1/B0/B1 are closed-form regularised dense linear maps, not trained networks: A reads E per port (W @ Emap), B reads per-bin radiance (synthetic) or per-direction irradiance share (MIR). Suffix 0 = loss only on visible outputs (synthetic bins 0,1,4,5 of 12 per port; MIR 3 of 8 directions), suffix 1 = all outputs. Hidden outputs under visible-only supervision are set by a graph-Laplacian term over the output bins of the same port (harmonic extension; lambda 1e-6, eps 1e-9). No optimiser, no shared parameters, no nonlinearity.

WL47 MIR Stage C training and test targets are synthesised linearly from the rendered basis matrix T1 (32 outputs x 16 inputs, from 16 basis renders at 256 spp): Ytr = T1 @ L with no added noise. The independent basis set T2 is used only for the reference noise floor. B1's 3e-6 held-out error on MIR is therefore recovery of a known linear map from 128 noise-free samples; Cycles enters through T1 and through the superposition check on the two pair fields.
implementation_facts.source: experiments/fnto_smoke47/stage_ac47.py:stage_c (run_regime('MIR', T1, ..., Tnoise=T2); Ttr defaults to T); eval_b47.py:mir

implementation_facts.claim: WL47 MIR fixture: closed black box 1.1 x 0.4 x 0.2 m, floor = Cycles Glossy GGX colour 0.9 roughness 0.25, four ceiling windows of x-width 0.1 m; inputs only through P0 and P1; 8 directions on one arc in the x-z plane (signed tan -1.5 ... 1.875), sun angle 0.5 deg; outputs = port-mean radiance at all 4 windows from 8 orthographic cameras (64x64, GAUSSIAN 0.01 point sampling); max_bounces 4; irradiance measured with rho=1 Lambert planes in the open windows.

WL47 SSS fixture: the Lego blend's own Yellow material copied with its Displacement link removed, on a 3 x 1 m plane under a shadow-only half-plane occluder (edge x=0); suns in the y-z plane, field A 0 deg strength 5, field B 60 deg strength 10 (both E=5); three cameras (top, +y 45, -y 45), 64 x 8 px, bounces 32. Material meta recorded: falloff BURLEY, radius (1.0, 0.2, 0.1), scale 1.

WL47 E-only floors: eonly_linear_floor = least-squares E->Y map fitted on the test set itself; eonly_pair_floor = sqrt(sum|YA-YB|^2 / 2 / (sum|YA|^2 + sum|YB|^2)), a lower bound for any function of E on the pair set.

The production composition (used unchanged by WL50/WL51) is an undamped fixed-point iteration: L <- I[hit] * valid (+ sun specular), where I = outgoing(E_ind(L)) applies the same K (rho/pi E_tot + kappa/pi E_ind + K_glob + K_mid + K_band) at every iteration. The sender value is one RGB value per port; band and mid weights are precomputed with the outgoing direction set to the port normal; 128 cosine gathers per port. 'Diverged' = non-finite, or median residual ratio >= 1 over the last 5 iterations after iteration 8.

implementation_facts.claim: WL49/WL50 learned arm: N_arm(x)_c = sum_e exp(MLP(desc_e))_c * measure_e * area-mean E_tot over element e. Weights are non-negative by construction and the output is linear in the field and isotropic; there is no energy or passivity constraint. Network 9-64-64-64-3 (9,155 parameters), identical for L0 (K44's 96 band + 128 mid representatives) and L1 (DASQ elements).

WL50 composition: at Yellow ports (338,864 domain-A ports with material 0) a keep mask zeroes K44 band + mid and N_arm is added to the port's outgoing value I. That same I is both rendered at the camera and sent into C's gathers at every solver iteration, i.e. the operator fitted to the camera-vertex response is applied at every bounce.
WL50 training target: per-port mean of r = Cycles probe colour - K44 K_glob - K44 K_loc at Yellow probe pixels (fit 480 / val 120 / test 120 probe configurations).

Probe renders that supply the K targets wrap every material in Mix(Fac = max(IsCameraRay, Backfacing if glass else 0), black emission strength 0, original): a non-camera ray reaching an opaque or SSS surface sees black, so the target contains no free-space interreflection.

DASQ: Morton-ordered octree over Lego ports; for a receiver, a node is accepted as one element when cell diagonal <= alpha x distance to its centroid and the centroid lies within R = 30 cm; single-port nodes are leaves; self port excluded; feature = area-mean irradiance over a contiguous Morton range via prefix sums. The element set depends only on static port geometry.

WL49 direct exitance measurement: Cycles DIFFUSE bake with pass filter DIRECT + COLOR into a per-vertex colour attribute of the single Lego object under one sun (held-out T0 view 6, strength E_SUN = 5, angle 0); flux = pi x sum(triangle area x mean vertex radiance); the Yellow 2 % glossy is excluded. The incident-power denominator is the same bake with every material slot replaced by a white Lambertian.

WL48 Probe A queries the frozen K44 nonlocal output (glob + band + mid) toward the port normal, training-camera directions, C-requested directions, 19 bin centres and 64 cosine directions. Its energy ratio is sum(A_port x pi x mean over 64 cosine directions of L) / sum(A_port x E_sun) over Lego ports (port areas, 200k-port subsample).

WL50 refcheck scene is a uniformly sun-lit 1 x 1 m Yellow plane (displacement removed, pure Burley in run 2b) with a white Lambert patch at 0.3 / 0.6 m; it compares patch irradiance with a prediction integrated from the camera-seen plane radiance.

WL51 SEM counterfactual overrides only the value Yellow ports send into C: I[yellow] = 0.98 x (0.7991, 0.5029, 0.0296)/pi x E_tot + sum(kappa)/pi x E_ind. Receiver and render terms are untouched. Because the override discards the arm, the sender and therefore rho are identical for H / L0C / L1C.

WL51 rho estimator: per-channel power iteration of the homogeneous composed map (sun off), 40 iterations, fp16 state renormalised to norm 1e3 per channel, rho_c = median of the last 10 norm ratios. Class-reduced rho = spectral radius of M x diag(g), with M the class-to-class return fraction and g the out/in flux gain, both on port areas. Edge masks zero valid / spec / L on masked (receiver port, gather) edges.

WL51 Gate 2 scene: two closed 0.4 x 0.4 m Yellow slabs, 4 mm thick, 4 mm air gap; J = one object, S = identical vertices as two objects; sun angle 0; a 10 cm patch 0.1 m above the top face, invisible to shadow / diffuse / glossy / transmission rays, as white Lambert (Yellow then has a diffuse ancestor) or roughness-0 mirror (singular ancestor); 1024 spp camera views, 4096 spp patches, seeds 5101 / 5102; chain control L_above uses plain Lambert 0.98 x colour.

Cycles 3.5.1 kernel: for CLOSURE_BSSRDF_BURLEY the radius is set to 0 when PATH_RAY_DIFFUSE_ANCESTOR is set (svm/closure.h:903-926); a channel with radius below BSSRDF_MIN_RADIUS becomes a Lambertian DiffuseBsdf (closure/bssrdf.h:300-333); the subsurface bounce clears PATH_RAY_CAMERA and the exit point gets a DiffuseBsdf (integrator/subsurface.h:49, 98); a LABEL_DIFFUSE bounce sets PATH_RAY_DIFFUSE_ANCESTOR (integrator/path_state.h:183-184). The Lego is one object with 8 material slots; Yellow = Mix(0.02, SSS Burley, Glossy 0.3) and is the only SSS material.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Collapsing incoming radiance to irradiance is an information limit (not a fitting limit) where intrinsic transport is direction-selective.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Two constructed fixtures: synthetic S1 (32 pairs) and a Cycles rough-mirror cavity (2 pairs, 8 directions on one arc). Equal-E pairs (delta-E <= 5e-6) give outputs differing by 0.98-1.11 at noise 2e-5; the best E-only linear map fitted on the test set has 0.87-0.90 error; pair floor for any function of E 0.59-0.68. The limit follows from identical inputs mapping to different outputs, so it holds for any E-only model on these fixtures.

worklog_interpretations.claim: A direction-aware operator recovers the transport, but only with full-boundary supervision; visible-only supervision gives wrong, non-passive hidden outputs; the two factors are synergistic and neither suffices alone.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: For a dense closed-form linear map with a harmonic-extension rule for unsupervised outputs: B1 1.4e-5 (S1) / 3e-6 (MIR, on targets synthesised from the rendered basis matrix); B0 hidden error 1.057 / 1.033 and S1 column albedo 1.77; interaction -0.86 to -1.07. It is a property of this surrogate and its predeclared extension rule; no shared-parameter or nonlinear learner was tested (stated in the worklog).

worklog_interpretations.claim: Learning capacity / optimisation is not the limiting factor in the surrogate.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Closed-form fits with 128 configurations for 48 / 16 input dimensions identify the map exactly. Says nothing about K44 or any network (worklog states this).

worklog_interpretations.claim: For Lego Yellow (Cycles Burley SSS) the incoming angular collapse is not the missing information; irradiance suffices within the measured uncertainty.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL47 verdict row 3 and case classification (CASE 4); repeated in WL48 'sufficient evidence' list as 'Yellow incoming angular information is unnecessary'
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One pair of fields (0 vs 60 deg in one azimuth plane) on a flat plane with displacement removed; R <= 1.0 %, G <= 1.9 % within bounds of 2.3 % / 6.2 %; blue inconclusive beyond 6 cm; bands hold 5-29 pixels. WL48's wording 'unnecessary' is stronger than the bounded two-angle measurement.

worklog_interpretations.claim: K44's directional-sender failure is not mainly a hidden-supervision effect; it is a direction artefact concentrated at the port normal (5-9x low) plus an energy level above passivity.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL48 answer table and Probe A interpretation; verdict B
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Frozen K44 queries: requested / cosine-mean 0.995-1.009, requested / normal 5.2-9.2, supervised vs unsupervised direction deviation ratio 1.07-1.15, never / observed port anisotropy 1.49 / 1.50 (rule 1.5 met in one of two views). The origin of the normal deficit was not localised.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Physical passivity and reference fidelity conflict for Yellow under Cycles' object-scoped Burley on this geometry; K44's excess energy is not by itself a K defect.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL48 Probe A inference (P1, post hoc); confirmed in magnitude by WL49 Gate 0
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: WL48: oracle extrapolation 4.8x (scale fitted on visible pixels). WL49: direct Cycles bake, Yellow exit flux 3.92x the sun power incident on the whole Lego mesh and 8.1x that incident on Yellow, red, one sun direction, replicate 0.6 %. The conflict statement itself is an inference from flux > incident power; WL51 later shows the non-passive response exists only at no-diffuse-ancestor vertices.

worklog_interpretations.claim: K44's in-support band / mid representative aggregation is the binding capacity limit for Yellow nonlocal transport; the 30 cm support plus a rank-64 tail is adequate.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL48 Probe B interpretation; WL49 Gate 1 interpretation
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Against a fitted Burley oracle (not Cycles): ideal-weight error 0.35 / 0.26 / 0.25 (WL48) and 0.51 / 0.36 / 0.33 on WL49's test fields; valid fits no better than 0.56 / 0.23 / 0.22; collision floor B 0.225; representatives cover 29 % of the red in-support shadow response; support + rank-64 leaves 0.008.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The WL46 glossy-scene over-brightness and edit degradation come from reading K44's Yellow sender off-normal, not from the 19-bin basis.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL48 Probe C interpretation; verdict H (INCONCLUSIVE)
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Basis vs exact reads differ by -0.2 dB and <= 0.005 edit correlation (measured, excludes the basis). The K-side cause is inferred from the 4x rise of Yellow's plane contribution; no known-field reference for that scene exists.

worklog_interpretations.claim: DASQ removes most of the aggregation limit and its advantage is not a parameter-count effect.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Oracle space: quadrature 0.044 / 0.054 / 0.122 at 2.2-2.8x elements; identical 9,155-parameter network gives L1 0.044 / 0.067 / 0.198 vs L0 0.319 / 0.194 / 0.261 (formally INCONCLUSIVE: L1 misses the 2 % plateau rule). Real scene first event +0.65 dB, capped by the oracle (L1 ~ oracle 24.8 dB). No coupled solve.

worklog_interpretations.claim: DASQ's spatial advantage transfers to a complete FNTO K at first event but does not survive repeated GI composition; the failure is not DASQ-specific.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL50 answer and verdicts B, C, E
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: L1C - L0C +0.51 / +0.29 dB (rule missed by 0.015 dB on one seed); 64/64 coupled solves diverge for both arms and both seeds, rho 6.9-9.0 vs 0.55; L0C diverges too.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The divergence is caused by an ownership overlap: object-scoped Burley already transports light between surfaces of the same object and C transports the same Yellow-to-Yellow paths again; a camera/indirect reference mismatch is excluded.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Only that the loop is Yellow<->Yellow (99.8 %) and that a uniformly lit plane gives patch / prediction 1.0-1.2. WL51 shows the plane test could not discriminate and that the reference does differ by path vertex; WL51 rejects the path-duplication reading in renderer path space.

worklog_interpretations.claim: K44 converges only because its band / mid sender is 5-9x low at the port normal, with K_glob carrying the Yellow red output.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: H mode: K_glob 86 % of the Yellow red sender, band + mid 2 %; H Yellow gain 0.65; production sender uses normal-direction band / mid weights (code); WL48 normal deficit 5-9x. No run of K44 with a corrected-direction sender inside the production solve exists in this scope (WL46 reported divergence for a directional in-solve sender).

worklog_interpretations.claim: Cycles 3.5.1 applies the object-scoped Burley BSSRDF only at vertices without a diffuse ancestor; after a diffuse or SSS-exit bounce Yellow is Lambert 0.98 x colour (0.783 / 0.493 / 0.029).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Source-code reading (on the server's bpy install, not in the repo) plus the slab render: diffuse-ancestor patch receives exactly 0 where a camera sees 0.845; mirror-ancestor ratio 0.99-1.00; Lambert chain control 1.000. One geometry, two seeds; the Lambert value itself (0.783) is from the source and the SEM formula, not separately measured as an albedo.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The divergence is high-gain recurrence of a vertex-specific reference operator through disjoint paths, not a duplicated K/C path: rho = Yellow gain x Yellow->Yellow return.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Target provenance from the probe mask (no free-space paths in the target); Yellow<-Yellow edges necessary and sufficient for rho > 1; class reduction g x M = 8.08 x 0.851 = 6.888 and 10.47 x 0.857 = 8.982 matches the full rho; substituting the Lambert interior sender gives rho 0.79 and 48/48 converged solves. 'Disjoint' refers to renderer path space; overlap relative to the intended physical contract is left INCONCLUSIVE (air-chord proxy only).

worklog_interpretations.claim: A single vertex-independent intrinsic K trained on first-event references cannot match this reference with a convergent composition; a reference-consistent decomposition must distinguish observed-vertex and interior-vertex operators, or the reference must change.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL51 verdict G and 'Characterised contract mismatch'
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Three operator variants only: reference-faithful arms diverge (rho 6.9-9.0); K44 converges with Yellow indirect 1.74x and corr 0.25; the diagnostic two-operator SEM converges with 0.72-0.75x and corr 0.77-0.83. The impossibility statement follows from the class reduction (camera-vertex gain 8.1 x return 0.85 > 1 for any operator that reproduces the target), not from an exhaustive test; the two-operator decomposition was run only as a diagnostic override, never as a trained model.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The arms reproduce the reference camera-vertex gain they were trained on.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Arm first-event Yellow gain (port areas) 9.71 / 11.10 (view 6) and 8.07 / 8.95 (view 15) against a Cycles bake of 8.10 for view 6 only (mesh areas, glossy excluded). Same order of magnitude; the arms are 20-37 % above the bake in view 6 and the difference is not attributed.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The Yellow-halves reciprocity asymmetry (1.14 / 0.87) and the 1.45-1.5x port/mesh area inflation cannot drive the instability.
worklog_interpretations.source: WL51 Gate 3 and INTERPRETATION 'Interface / accounting error: minor'
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Closure <= 0.87 per class; the asymmetric pair carries 3.5-4 % of Yellow emission; class-reduced rho reproduces the full rho. The cancellation of the area inflation is an argument (same measure in numerator and denominator), and the 73 % same-half return cannot be checked by reciprocity (stated).

worklog_interpretations.claim: 57-59 % of the camera-vertex Burley red response at Yellow receivers arrives through chords that leave the surface into air, i.e. transport that the intended contract assigns to C.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A geometric dot-product proxy on the fitted Burley oracle with no inside test; the one direct observation is the slab: one-object top face 0.845 vs two-object ~0 across a 4 mm air gap.

contradictions.between: WL50 interpretation vs WL51
contradictions.description: WL50 concluded from its plane refcheck that indirect rays see the camera-seen Burley radiance ('not a camera / indirect reference mismatch') and inferred a K/C ownership overlap. WL51 shows by source reading and the slab render that the reference does differ by path vertex (diffuse ancestor -> Lambert) and classes path overlap as NOT SUPPORTED in renderer path space. WL51 records this as an explicit correction; WL50 is left unedited.

contradictions.between: WL50 refcheck numbers vs WL50's reading of them
contradictions.description: The refcheck red ratio was 1.157 (h 0.3 m) and 1.217 (h 0.6 m), reported as 'ratio 1.0-1.2' and read as agreement. The Lambert interior value 0.98 x 0.799 x E/pi = 1.246 exceeds the plane's camera-seen centre radiance 1.176 by 6 %, so a red excess above 1 is in the direction WL51's rule predicts (this reader's arithmetic from refcheck.json; the remaining excess and its growth with height are not explained in either worklog).

contradictions.between: WL50 Gate 3 attribution vs WL51 Gate 1
contradictions.description: WL50 describes a red-channel loop and reports G / B as 'decayed below fp16' (NaN in diag.json). WL51's per-channel renormalised iteration shows green is unstable as well: rho_G 4.288 (L0C) and 5.138 (L1C); only blue is stable (0.40).

contradictions.between: WL45 / WL48 / WL49 on Yellow energy
contradictions.description: WL45 called K44's Yellow first-bounce power 'beyond any physical bound' and treated it as a K-side anomaly. WL48 (oracle extrapolation 4.8x) and WL49 (direct bake 3.9x) show the reference itself exceeds the bound, so the excess is not by itself a K defect. WL51 then narrows it: the non-passive response exists only at no-diffuse-ancestor vertices; the interior operator is passive (0.78).

contradictions.between: energy ratios across WL48 / WL49 / WL50 / WL51
contradictions.description: The ratios use different measures: WL48 4.3-4.6x and P1 4.8x are port-area flux over port-area Lego sun power; WL49's 3.9x is mesh-area flux over mesh-area incident power (3.44x on the port denominator); WL50 compares its port-based 4.1-4.9x with 'the WL49 bake 3.9x'; WL51 compares port-based arm gains 9.7-11.1 with the mesh-based bake 8.1. Port areas are 1.45x (Yellow) to 1.51x (Lego) the mesh areas, so the comparisons are approximate, and component sets differ (bake excludes the 2 % glossy; arm sender flux includes K_loc and K_glob).

contradictions.between: WL51 statement vs its own table
contradictions.description: 'The arms reproduce the reference camera-vertex gain they were trained on' against first-event gains of 9.71 (L0C) and 11.10 (L1C) for view 6 where the bake is 8.10: +20 % and +37 %. Likewise WL50 calls 4.1-4.9x 'approximately the WL49 bake 3.9x' (+6 to +24 %).

contradictions.between: WL49 real-scene band result vs WL50 complete-K result
contradictions.description: WL49 Gate 4: in the 3-30 cm shadow band the oracle-trained L1 beats K44 (24.12 vs 21.62 dB). WL50 Gate 1: the complete K with the Cycles-residual-trained arm does not (L1C 21.47 / 21.33 vs H 21.62); the complete-K gain sits in lit, overall shadow and never-observed receivers instead.

contradictions.between: WL49 oracle-space learned gain vs WL50 Cycles-residual gain
contradictions.description: L1 over L0 is 65-86 % (R / G) on the noise-free Burley oracle target but 1-2 % relative on the Cycles probe residual, where no arm explains most of the target (test rel L2 0.86 / 0.60 / 0.63). WL50 attributes this to probe noise and non-nonlocal residue without separating them.

contradictions.between: WL49 verdict vs WL50 Gate 0
contradictions.description: WL49 holds the learned comparison formally INCONCLUSIVE because L1 missed the 2 % plateau rule (14-15 %). WL50 reclassifies the fluctuation as stochastic variation after inspecting the last four evaluations (final two differ < 0.3 %) while leaving WL49's verdict unchanged.

contradictions.between: WL48 Probe B predeclared criterion vs post hoc readout
contradictions.description: 'fitting_accounts' is TRUE with the predeclared normal-direction readout (0.712 >= 2 x 0.339) and would be FALSE with the hemispherical mean (0.517 < 0.678). The normal readout is confounded by the Probe A normal-direction artefact; both are reported.

contradictions.between: WL47 text vs code
contradictions.description: WL47 says 'K_band takes a 7-bin incident partition'; the code has N_BINS_H = 19. WL48 records the correction; no WL47 measurement depends on it.

contradictions.between: WL47 surrogate vs WL48 on hidden-direction supervision
contradictions.description: WL47: without supervision of hidden (port, direction) outputs a direction-aware linear map is wrong and non-passive there. WL48: for frozen K44 the invalid sender is not associated with supervision (direction 1.07-1.15x, port 1.49 / 1.50), and the fault is a normal-direction deficit plus reference-level energy. The two are different model classes; WL48 states the surrogate result is unchanged, so the WL47 finding has no confirmed counterpart in K44.

contradictions.between: WL51 SEM result vs reference
contradictions.description: SEM is described as reproducing the renderer's path set without duplication, yet its coupled Yellow indirect is 0.72-0.75x the reference with correlation 0.77-0.83, and it treats Yellow after glossy/singular ancestors as Lambert where Cycles keeps Burley. The shortfall is unattributed.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: An operator that is applied recursively must have loop gain below 1 on the fields its own composition returns to it; fidelity to a single-application (first-event) target does not provide this, and fitting a non-passive target faithfully makes divergence the expected outcome when the return fraction is high.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL50: first-event gain +0.3-0.5 dB, then 64/64 divergent solves per arm and seed. WL51: rho equals Yellow gain x Yellow->Yellow return (8.08 x 0.851 = 6.888; 10.47 x 0.857 = 8.982); return fraction is 0.77 even for uniform emission.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The supervision target must be the operator that the composition actually applies at that position in a path. If the reference renderer's response depends on path history, a single history-independent operator fitted to camera-vertex responses is a different operator from the one the reference uses at interior vertices.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL51 slab render: camera vertex 0.845, diffuse-ancestor vertex exactly 0, mirror-ancestor 0.99-1.00; substituting the interior operator alone moves rho from 6.9-9.0 to 0.79 and Yellow indirect correlation from 0.25 to 0.77-0.83.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The specific trigger (Burley BSSRDF disabled after a diffuse ancestor, object-scoped entry sampling) is a property of Cycles 3.5.1 BSSRDF closures; it constrains any use of that reference, not learned operators as such.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL51 Gate 0 source facts and Gate 2; one-object vs two-object slab 0.845 vs ~0 across a 4 mm air gap.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Non-negative weights and linearity in the input field do not imply passivity; an energy bound has to be measured or enforced separately.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: The WL49/WL50 arms use exp() weights times a positive measure (non-negative, linear) and still have Yellow gain 8.1-10.5 and rho 6.9-9.0.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Convergence of a composed system does not certify its operator: a stable solve can result from an unrelated deficit.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: K44 converges (rho 0.55) with a sender 5-9x low at the port normal and K_glob carrying 86 % of the Yellow red mode; its coupled Yellow indirect is 1.74x the reference with correlation 0.25.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Composed behaviour has to be evaluated on the composed operator (spectral radius, single flight, coupled solve); neither first-event PSNR nor oracle-space error predicted it.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL49 and WL50 first-event gains for L1 / L1C; one flight 4.0-4.2x the all-bounce reference; all coupled solves diverged.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Scalar irradiance as the incident representation is insufficient where intrinsic transport is direction-selective: equal-irradiance inputs then have different outputs and no function of irradiance can separate them.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL47 S1 and the Cycles mirror cavity: output difference 0.98-1.11 at delta-E <= 5e-6; E-only pair floor 0.59-0.68.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: For the Lego Yellow Burley SSS regime, incident angular information is not required within 1-2 % (bounds 2.3 % red, 6.2 % green) for the tested pair of angles.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL47 SSS: 0 vs 60 deg at equal irradiance, 3-30 cm bands, no SENSITIVE cell; blue inconclusive beyond 6 cm.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Outputs in directions or at ports that receive no supervision are not determined by supervision elsewhere; in the tested surrogate they were both wrong and non-passive, and direction-aware input only helped together with full-boundary supervision.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL47 B0: hidden error 1.03-1.06, S1 column albedo 1.77, interaction -0.86 to -1.07. Tested only for a dense linear map with a harmonic-extension rule; WL48 found no supervision association for K44's invalid sender.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The value a coupling stage reads from a sender must be evaluated with the semantics the coupling uses (direction requested); reading a fixed normal-direction value changed the Yellow contribution by about 5x.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL48: requested / normal 5.2-9.2; Yellow share of the glossy-plane reflection 0.22-0.27 with normal reads vs 0.86-1.12 off-normal; per-ray normal / exact 0.19-0.20.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A fixed representative subset of source aggregates loses information that no downstream weight model can recover; coverage of the whole support was what removed the error, at 2.2-2.8x the element count.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL49: representatives cover 29 % of the red in-support shadow response; collision floor B 0.225; valid fits >= 0.22 in every channel; DASQ quadrature 0.044 / 0.054 / 0.122; budget-matched variant infeasible. Oracle is a fitted Burley on one object.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A comparison between representations needs a target whose noise and unexplained residue are below the effect being measured.

open_confounds: WL47 MIR Stage C is identification of a 32 x 16 linear map from noise-free targets synthesised from the rendered basis; it is not a test of learning from rendered samples, of a shared-parameter operator, or of a nonlinear model.

WL47 B0's hidden-output failure and non-passivity depend on the predeclared harmonic-extension rule; whether a structured shared operator extrapolates passively to unsupervised (port, direction) outputs was not tested.

The direction-selective share of the real Lego scene's intrinsic transport (glass internal reflection / transmission) is unmeasured; glass indirect stays at 0.07-0.16x of the reference in every WL50 / WL51 condition and transmission was out of scope throughout.

The Yellow angle-insensitivity rests on one angle pair in one azimuth plane, a flat plane with displacement (bump normals) removed, Burley only (no random-walk SSS), bands of 5-29 pixels, and blue inconclusive beyond 6 cm; one resolved 0.6 % red difference is unattributed.
The Cycles kernel source lines behind the diffuse-ancestor rule are not in the repository and were not re-read here; the empirical confirmation is one slab geometry at two seeds.

The SEM counterfactual's remaining Yellow indirect shortfall (0.72-0.75x, correlation 0.77-0.83) is unattributed between Yellow seen after glossy / singular ancestors (Burley in Cycles, Lambert in SEM) and C's own gathered-field deficit (WL45 0.76-0.89x).

The share of the reference Yellow indirect that arrives via glossy / singular ancestors is unmeasured, so how closely a two-operator (observed / interior) decomposition could match the reference is unknown; such a decomposition was never trained, only substituted diagnostically.
The share of the camera-vertex Burley response that crosses air is known only from a geometric proxy (57-59 % red) without an inside test or object-split renders on the Lego.

The arms' first-event Yellow gain exceeds the direct bake (9.7-11.1 vs 8.1, view 6); port-area vs mesh-area measure, inclusion of K_loc / K_glob / glossy, isotropic-exit assumption and fit error are not separated. The bake exists for one sun direction only.

WL50's probe residual: the split between Cycles pixel noise and non-nonlocal residue (K_loc / K_glob fit error) in the 0.60-0.87 unexplained relative L2 is not separated; it bounds what any arm comparison on that target can show.

The capacity results of WL48 / WL49 are against a fitted object-scoped Burley oracle (three scale factors fitted on visible pixels of views 0-7), not Cycles; the real-scene gain is capped at the oracle's own 24.8 dB.
WL49's learned comparison is formally INCONCLUSIVE (L1 plateau rule missed); WL50's +0.3 dB both-seed criterion was missed by 0.015 dB.
The origin of K44's normal-direction deficit (band / mid outgoing-direction conditioning never supervised at the normal, or other) is not localised.

The K-side cause of the WL46 glossy-scene over-brightness and edit degradation is inferred; no known-field reference for that scene exists, and importance-sampling / analytic-plane semantics are not separated from K.

rho is a norm-growth estimate on fp16 state with per-channel renormalisation; K44's operator is not elementwise non-negative (removing edges raised H's rho from 0.549 to 0.576), and the mask results show which edges carry the feedback, not that they were double counted (stated in the protocol).
Under SEM the mode's Yellow->Yellow return fraction is 0.988, against 0.77 for uniform emission; stability there rests on the interior albedo 0.78 alone, on port areas that sum to 1.45x the mesh.
All composition evidence is one scene (Lego + box), one SSS material, one edit, held-out T0; mode statistics and view results use arm seed 5011 only (seed 5012 for unmasked rho only).
The KF pixel-origin arms carry an unexplained bias / outlier population (+12-14 %, correlation -0.12) at every kappa.

Whether DASQ can reach the existing element budget (2.2-2.8x now; axis-aligned octree, not surface-adaptive) and its per-iteration cost (0.36 s, 23x L0C) inside any convergent composition are untested.

Whether any single history-independent operator could be both convergent and close to this reference was argued from the gain x return reduction and three operator variants, not tested exhaustively; the alternative of a path-history-independent reference lies outside this scope (WL53).
narrative_summary:
WL47 tested, on constructed fixtures, whether collapsing incident boundary radiance to scalar irradiance loses information. In a synthetic internal-mirror oracle (S1) and a Cycles rough-mirror cavity (MIR), pairs of fields with equal per-port irradiance (matched to 5e-6 or better) produced nonlocal outputs differing by 0.98-1.11 at noise 2e-5, and the best irradiance-only linear map fitted on the test set still had 0.87-0.90 error. The control oracle S0 and the Lego Yellow Burley material showed no such effect (red <= 1.0 %, green <= 1.9 %, one 0/60 degree pair, flat plane, displacement removed, blue inconclusive). The "learned operators" are closed-form dense linear maps; with direction-resolved input they recover the transport only when every output is supervised. With visible-only supervision the unsupervised outputs, filled by a harmonic-extension rule, were wrong (1.03-1.06) and non-passive (albedo 1.77). The MIR fit used targets synthesised from the rendered basis matrix.

WL48 found that frozen K44's Yellow nonlocal sender is near-isotropic except for a 5-9x deficit at the port normal, which is the direction the production solver reads; supervision coverage did not explain it. It also found K44's in-support representative aggregation to be a capacity bound against a Burley oracle. WL49 measured directly that Cycles' Yellow first-event exit flux is 3.9x the sun power incident on the whole Lego mesh (8.1x that on Yellow), and showed that a distance-adaptive full-coverage quadrature (DASQ) removes most of the aggregation error at 2.2-2.8x the elements, with a +0.65 dB first-event gain in the real scene.

WL50 placed matched learned arms (existing aggregation and DASQ) inside the unchanged K/C solver. First-event Yellow fidelity improved (+0.51 / +0.29 dB over the matched arm), but every coupled solve diverged for both arms and seeds (rho 6.9-9.0 against 0.55). WL50 attributed this to K/C path overlap.

WL51 replaced that attribution. The K target contains no free-space transport, because probe renders blacken every non-camera hit. Cycles 3.5.1 applies the object-scoped Burley BSSRDF only at vertices without a diffuse ancestor; elsewhere Yellow is Lambert with albedo 0.78 / 0.49 / 0.03. A slab render confirmed it: a diffuse-ancestor patch received exactly 0 where a camera saw 0.845, and a mirror-ancestor patch saw 0.99-1.00. The arms learn the camera-vertex operator, whose gain on Yellow is 8-10 in red, and the solver applies it at every bounce; with 85 % of Yellow flux returning to Yellow, rho equals gain times return (6.888, 8.982). Substituting the Lambert interior sender alone gave rho 0.79, 48/48 converged solves and Yellow indirect at 0.72-0.75x the reference (correlation 0.77-0.83), a diagnostic that leaves a shortfall unattributed.

For any operator that is composed or iterated, this scope shows three things. First-event fidelity did not predict coupled behaviour. Non-negative, linear weights did not give passivity. K44's convergence came from an unrelated sender deficit, not from a valid operator. The training target also has to be the operator the composition applies at that path position, which a path-history-dependent reference cannot supply to a single history-independent K. The evidence is one scene, one SSS material and one renderer semantics.

implementation_facts.claim: WL52 learned C (GLT) is E_ind(r) = sum_s F_rs * Lbar_s with F_r = pi * softmax([l_null, log(FF0_rs/pi) + g_phi]); logits are -inf where the analytic unoccluded FF0 is 0. It is linear in the source radiance, non-negative and row-sum <= pi by construction. Evaluation is dense receiver x patch (F is an [N, M] float tensor); 923,010 parameters (6-layer d=128 transformer on patch tokens + pair head on 10 relative-geometry features). No rays are used by the operator.

GLT's source representation is the AREA-MEAN radiance per patch (4 x 4 ports of ~3.1 cm = ~12.5 cm); receivers are ports. Inference runs under bfloat16 autocast in chunks of 2048 receivers. The control arm C0p is the ray-traced transfer on the same patch representation (pi * 1024-gather hit histogram over patches), so C1 - C0p isolates what learning adds on top of the representation.

WL52 explicit baseline C0 = Mitsuba (cuda_ad_rgb) scene/BVH build + 128 cosine gathers per port (4 sample points x 32 directions), front-face hit -> port id by an on-device triangle-to-port lookup, application E = pi/K * sum L[hit]. The benchmark 'C0 update' is BVH build + gather; 'C1 update' is encoder + dense F. The C1 frame time still includes the BVH build because sun visibility and the camera lookup need it (only the relation table is replaced).

WL52 Stage A's '0.105 s for 109 M rays' is NOT an end-to-end GPU relation build: it is the extrapolation of a trace-only probe of 2^24 random rays inside the scene bounding box (no port ray setup, no hit -> port mapping). The '277 s production path' is extrapolated from a 100,000-port subset of 854,060 ports.

WL53 intrinsic-K oracle TR: Monte Carlo RTE inside ONE isolated domain (index-matched boundary, homogeneous sigma_t, RGB albedo weight, isotropic/HG phase, Russian roulette); photons are recorded at their FIRST exit into air into (port, out-bin); the camera operator KC is next-event estimation at every collision and excludes the unscattered term; accumulators are float64 (amendment 2). Mitsuba is used only as a ray-triangle intersector.

Oracle K sampling cost is set by construction: one unit-flux source per (port, in-bin) cell with n_per photons, so photons = P_cells * Din * n_per (slab 240 ports x 16 bins x 2048 = 7.86 M at 1 cm; 3840 cells -> 125.8 M at 2.5 mm). WL53 stores T dense as (3, P*Dout, P*Din); WL55 stores it sparse (one entry per photon exit, coalesced in float64, CSR at apply time), so nnz is bounded by the photon count rather than by intrinsic sparsity.

Explicit C in WL53-56 is a pure ray cast: M rays per out-cell (port, out-bin) from the outward hemisphere, only front-face first hits are recorded into (port', in-bin) with weight 1/M, misses go to an escape fraction; same-domain re-entry is part of C. Composition is the undamped fixed point phi_in = phi_ext + C phi_out, phi_out = K phi_in (tolerance 1e-7); Lambert K = rho * (sum of in-flux) / Dout.

WL53's spectral-radius estimator is a last-norm-ratio power iteration; WL54 replaced it with power iteration on A^2 (rho_robust) because a +/- eigenvalue pair (bipartite coupling) invalidates the last-ratio estimate.

CASP level rule is geometry-only: 256 cosine rays per coarse port, nu = fraction of hits closer than 4h; nu < 0.05 keeps one unknown; otherwise level = clamp(2^ceil(log2(c*h / median near-hit distance)), 1, 8) with c = 2. Cells are cut by triangle-wise affine subdivision (exact surface); the caster is cast_C with per-port ray counts (weight 1/count).

CAK's K on adaptive cells is K_cells = R_out K_fine P_in: a cell's in-flux is distributed over its 2.5 mm sub-cells by current area (same in-bin) and fine out-cells are summed (same out-bin). A rigid move therefore needs only re-levelling and re-aggregation of the stored 2.5 mm operator, no new TR.

The ballistic camera term KB is, per output port, the projected-area mean of exp(-sigma_t * s) / (A_j * pi / Din) for the backward camera ray leaving the medium through in-cell j and bin b (4096 samples per port), assuming in-cell radiance uniform over cell and bin.

WL56's dirty set is an exact whole-domain test: SHA-256 over canonical material mesh, current intrinsic vertices, medium parameters, level and bin counts, with placement excluded; dirty(state) = domains whose signature differs from rest (dent -> [upper], rigid -> []). The unit of selection is a complete optical domain; there is no partial-domain selection and no learned selector.

In WL56 arm F actually runs TR for both domains and arm S only for dirty domains (clean package loaded from cache and re-hashed); every arm then rebuilds boundary cells, CSR operators, C (cast_adaptive), the incident field from 64 M emitter rays, K applied to the external field, the coupled solve and the readouts. No previously solved radiance is reused. Timings are CUDA-synchronised per component; the rho and validation diagnostics are timed separately and excluded from the update total; identity hashing is inside the package time.

WL53's non-rigid Delta-K statistics (Frobenius ratio, rank90, energy by distance, same-face share) are computed on the direction-summed port-pair matrix at 1 cm ports (240 x 240); only the rigid test also compares the full direction-resolved T. The dent 'support' is port centres with r < 2 cm + 3*L_d; for red (L_d 18.1 mm) that radius is 7.43 cm, which contains every port centre of the 10 x 10 cm slab, so the red in-support share of 1.00 is true by construction.

WL52 'visibility-transition ports' are ports whose 2048-gather oracle hit table differs in more than 10 % of the gathers between consecutive trajectory frames; the coupled reference REF is a path-traced E_ind at the ports (2 x 512 paths, 16 bounces, exact hit points, a shadow ray per vertex).

WL56 fixture: two 10 x 10 x 1 cm index-matched slabs (sigma_t 1000 /m, albedo 0.999/0.99/0.9) with an 8 mm air gap, upper slab dented (5 mm, radius 20 mm) or translated (+3.7, -2.1, +2.0) mm, a 20 x 20 cm downward Lambertian emitter, uniform 2.5 mm cells, 64 out / 16 in bins, 2048 photons per input cell (125,829,120 photons per domain build), 3 camera directions.
CASP maps to K conservatively (cell flux -> coarse port by sum, coarse flux -> cells by area weights) and therefore refines Lambert domains only; a port-resolved medium K keeps coarse unknowns.
