measurements.value: WL56: 175.3-178.9 s TR per domain (0.70-0.72 M photons/s), 180.2-183.7 s complete build wall, file 1.683 GB incl. ~0.531 GB KC, 57.6 M nnz. WL53: 7.9 M photons 70 s (4 camera directions), 1.26e8 photons without camera operators 106 s, peak 8.7 GB; Cycles reference set 3.3 h on 16 cores
measurements.conditions: WL56: 3 camera directions, idle GPU; WL53: dense accumulators, GPU shared with WL52 training

measurements.what: Runtime cost with a resident K (WL55 arms)
measurements.value: Per-iteration K + C application 0.90-0.99 ms (1 cm), 1.0-2.2 ms (CAK), 2.3-3.8 ms (2.5 mm); C application alone 0.41-0.51 ms; C build 13.6-39.8 ms; re-aggregation from K_fine 0.25-1.42 s; full composition incl. ballistic operator 0.23-0.54 s; 38-68 iterations
measurements.conditions: 480-18,240 cells, K nnz 5.3-57.6 M per domain, idle GPU

measurements.what: CAK coupled accuracy and tractability
measurements.value: Ruled groups passing 3 %: gap8 27/40 (1 cm) -> 33/40 (CAK) vs 34/40 (2.5 mm); gap4 20 -> 28 vs 28 of 34; floor 16 -> 18 of 18; bend90 21/21; held-out gap6s 23 -> 30 vs 30 of 33. Recovery of the 2.5 mm gain: 0.88 / 1.00 / 0.64 / 0.63 / 1.04 at 15 / 45 / 10 / 8 / 45 % of the 2.5 mm cells (rule >= 0.80 at <= 50 % failed)
measurements.conditions: nee + KB readout, 0.5 mm references; remaining failures are oblique groups

measurements.what: Selective vs full update, end to end
measurements.conditions: 2 domains, 1 dirty (dent) or 0 dirty (rigid); warm process, idle RTX 3090; uniform 2.5 mm cells

measurements.what: Cost split of the selective dent update
measurements.value: Package work 187.85 s of 188.93 s: dirty-domain TR 175.50 s (92.89 % of S), complete new package 183.71 s (97.24 %), ~3.3 s content hash per 1.68 GB package, clean-cache load 0.34 s. Shared current-state work 1.09 s: boundary 0.112, CSR / host->GPU 0.297, explicit C 0.035, 64 M source rays 0.146, K on external field 0.009, coupled solve 0.201 (51 iterations), readout 0.187, other 0.099 s. Residual if TR were free: 13.44 s
measurements.conditions: 8,080 cells, C nnz 1.34 M; peak GPU 4.45 GB, CPU RSS <= 5.82 GB

measurements.what: Resident rigid update split (no K work at all)
measurements.value: 0.685 s: boundary 0.110, C 0.020, incident field 0.145, K direct 0.003, solve 0.177 (45 iterations), readout 0.166, other 0.064 s
measurements.conditions: Second of 3 repeats; K already on GPU as CSR (initial CSR 0.337 s, initial cache load + check 7.93 s)

measurements.what: Exactness of selective recompute and physical accuracy of the oracle itself
measurements.value: F vs S max relative L1 1.55e-8; package content hashes identical. Both F and S pass 9/12 face-on channel tests; blue residuals +3.87 % (lower top), +3.57 % (upper bottom), +10.27 % (lower bottom); with the 64-bin readout the lower-bottom blue is +33.76 %. Source-seed change <= 0.269 points, C-seed change <= 0.022 points
measurements.conditions: Cycles 3.5.1 CUDA, 1024 spp, 0.5 mm pixels, 4 seeds; amended masks; 3 % + 3 SE rule

measurements.what: Stationary-receiver response and stale K
measurements.value: Reference change on the unchanged lower slab's top face: +2.23 / +4.06 / +2.19 % (whole face, signal/noise 72 / 150 / 189), +6.5 / +16.9 / +88.7 % in a fixed 25 mm disc. Predicted change slope F or S 1.040 / 0.996 / 0.975 (corr >= 0.9988); stale K slope 0.199 / 0.077 / 0.0098; relative L2 of the change error 0.80 / 0.92 / 0.99 (stale) vs 0.064 / 0.029 / 0.042 (S)
measurements.conditions: Bin readout in all arms; the lower domain's K is bit-identical between rest and dent

measurements.what: Break-even of domain selection as a function of per-domain K cost k (algebraic, post hoc A1)
measurements.value: Fixed raw-cache model T_F = 2k + 1.143 s, T_S = k + 5.219 s: >= 20 % saving needs k >= 7.17 s. Compact resident model T_F = 2k + H, T_S = k + H + O with H = 0.685 s (rigid measurement) and O = 0: k >= 0.228 s; speedup 1.0015x at k = 1 ms, 1.014x at 10 ms, 1.13x at 0.1 s, 1.59x at 1 s
measurements.conditions: Projection, not a measurement; H and O unmeasured for any compact or learned model; N = 2 domains only

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: computational overhead is the primary limiting factor of a learned C; explicit C on the GPU is already a few ms per geometry update.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One dense GLT (923k parameters, one seed) against a 128-gather GPU explicit C on synthetic Lambertian scenes of 5k-79k triangles and 2.5k-40k ports: 5.0 vs 44.0 ms at 10k ports, 11.1 vs 672 ms at 40k ports. Lego-scale explicit C was not run end to end on the GPU.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: the production Python relation build (277 s, 81 s incremental) is implementation overhead; the irreducible ray cost is 0.105 s.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: A trace-only throughput probe of 16.8 M random rays (1.04 G rays/s) scaled to 109 M rays; port ray setup and hit-to-port mapping on the device were not implemented or timed for the Lego scene; the Lego BVH build alone is 0.82 s.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: in FNTO the dominant cost is K (95 % of a step), not C.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One production solve with the K44 neural kernel on the Lego (854,060 ports): K outgoing 787 ms vs C 23.4 ms per iteration. It is a statement about K44's per-iteration application, not about K construction or about the oracle-K pipelines of WL53-56 (K + C application 1-4 ms).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: the localized errors are mostly inherited from the patch-level source representation; learning adds a smaller visibility-inference error.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: The ray-traced patch-transfer control C0p has near-contact p99 2.30 vs C1 2.32 and transition p99 1.32 vs 1.48; the C1 - C0p difference field has p99 0.79 / 0.67. The metric is post hoc; patch size was not varied.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: the P1 pass (+1.76 dB) is variance versus bias, not better transport.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Per-port E_ind error vs REF is worse for C1 (0.158) than C0 (0.112) while image PSNR is higher; REF's own split noise is 0.09-0.11, comparable to both errors, so the per-port ranking is close to the reference noise.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: the coarse-patch regime that keeps the learned C tractable is exactly the one that loses localized transport; a non-dense learned C might or might not beat ~5 ms.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Only one patch size and one dense architecture were trained; the top-k pruning attempt failed coverage before training. No finer-patch or sparse model exists.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL52: no memorization, generalization to unseen combinations and 2-3x object counts at the representation's level.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: First-event single-flight error C1 0.127 (test_iid) vs 0.160 (train_cfg, all ports); combo 0.142, scale_obj 0.203, each within 0.01-0.02 of C0p. One scene family, one seed.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL53: the ~5 % coupled-face miss comes from explicit C and its 1 cm port discretisation, not from K.
worklog_interpretations.source: docs/worklogs/53 'Answer', Gate 3 attribution (A3 / A4, post hoc)
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: An opaque Lambert box in place of the slab reproduced +6.2 % / +5.0 % and 64 incoming bins did not shrink the misses. WL54 and WL55 later split this into a real C-spatial part, a comparison artifact and a K-side boundary loss.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL53: rigid motion leaves K invariant; rigid reuse of K in material coordinates is exact up to noise.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One 37 deg rotation of the L-block at 2048 photons per cell: difference / seed noise 1.00-1.05 with seed noise ~0.9 % relative Frobenius, and composition differences <= 0.05 %. A dependence smaller than the noise level is not excluded; a 10 m translation exceeds noise through float32.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL53: a dent's K change is local and low-rank, a bend's is global and high-rank; nonlocal entries change relatively more than local ones.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Direction-summed port-pair matrices at 1 cm with 32768 photons per cell: dent rank90 8 / 8 / 18, bend90 133-151; dent in-support share 1.00 / 0.98 / 0.91, where the red value is vacuous (the support covers the whole slab). One dent, two bends, one slab.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL53: disjoint K/C path ownership composes stably; double-claiming a path family diverges.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Partition arms rho 0.42-0.82; one deliberate double-count control rho 4.75 / 2.92 / 0.83. The predeclared disjointness mapping itself was INCONCLUSIVE because the 3 % accuracy rule failed.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL54: with a local K the 1 cm near-contact error is spatial - convex sub-port structure of the source radiance, set at the first interreflection, mostly from pairs closer than a port.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: The exact-transfer coarse operator reproduces C0's error (attribution fraction 1.0-1.42); known-field averaging gives +17.6 % on gap4 with 94 % from pairs < 1 cm and ~0 for uniform, linear and step fields; ray count, seeds and bins contribute <= 0.4 % (+/- 3.3 % per realization).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL54: for a port-resolved medium K, C alone cannot fix the interface; the only lever is the resolution of K and C together.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: CASP equals C0 within 0.52 points on medium-medium links; a matched 5 mm oracle K and C halves the red / green gap-face errors and leaves blue at +3 to +5.5 %.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL54: the gap8 oblique lower-side group is a real transport under-prediction, presumably on the K side, and not a pixel-size effect.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Reference change +0.6 % between 0.5 and 0.25 mm pixels and no response to C refinement. WL55 attributes the group to the readout's missing ballistic term and shows the reference moves a further +5.0 % at 0.125 mm.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL55: 1 cm boundary ports lose physically important information on both sides of the K/C interface near contact, and the outgoing side dominates the coupled error.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Outgoing first-flight flux +9.7 to +22.3 % at 1 cm vs the continuous oracle, single-flight incident error up to +5.1 %, monotone convergence to <= +/- 1.8 % at 2.5 mm on 7 face-on groups. 'Dominates' is the author's comparison of these magnitudes, not a separate ablation.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL55: a contact-creating rigid move needs no new oracle when K is held at fine material resolution and re-aggregated to the current contact structure.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: One move (floor to 4 mm clearance): 18/18 groups with re-aggregation in 0.72 s vs 12/18 for the reused 1 cm interface. The Stage D rigid operator test formally missed its band (1.11 / 1.12 / 1.18, replicates 0.82 / 0.85 / 1.05).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL55: remaining oblique failures are mostly reference-limited (point-sampled pixels not converged), with one real held-out interface residual.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Oblique group signals move 3-20 % between 0.5 and 0.125 mm pixels and the continuous oracle shows the same residuals; convergence at 0.125 mm is not demonstrated, so the oblique verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL55: any learned or compressed K needs a target defined at an aggregation level where Delta-K is resolvable, and an aggregation-consistent hierarchy.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Delta-K / noise is 1.1-1.7 at 2.5 mm cell pairs and 3.6-8.1 at 1 cm ports with 2048 photons per cell; nothing learned was trained.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL56: selecting whole invalid optical domains preserves full-recompute output while a stationary receiver's GI changes (Gain A).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Bit-identical package content, F/S relative L1 1.55e-8, stationary-face change slope 0.975-1.040 vs stale 0.0098-0.199; one two-slab fixture, one dent, one translation.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL56: after exact selection the changed domain's TR (175.5 s, 92.89 % of S) is cost headroom for a within-domain rule/state mechanism (Gain B), not a demonstrated speedup.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: The cost split of the oracle update. Whether any cheaper within-domain mechanism reaches the oracle's accuracy was not tested; the oracle itself fails 3 of 12 channel tests.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL56: if K becomes cheap, incident-field generation, C, solve, readout and cache policy matter; C alone is not the dominant shared term; expensive-TR skip ratios cannot establish a neural-GI speedup.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Shared work 1.07-1.09 s per update (C 0.026-0.035 s) and a 0.685 s resident rigid update; the k-dependence is an algebraic projection with H and O unmeasured for any compact model.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL56: the blue floor (+3.6 to +10.3 %) lies between the fixed spatial / directional boundary approximation and intrinsic / readout estimation bias.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Source-seed and C-seed noise are excluded (<= 0.27 / 0.02 points) and the binned readout is shown to add error (+10.27 -> +33.76 %); no experiment separates the remaining candidates.

contradictions.between: WL53 interpretation vs WL54 / WL55 measurements
contradictions.description: WL53 states the ~5 % coupled-face miss 'comes from the explicit C and its 1 cm port discretization, not from K'. WL54 decomposes it into a real C-spatial error (box undersides), a comparison artifact (floor under the box: +1.2 % under full coverage instead of +3.9-5.2 %) and a K-side resolution dependency (medium gap faces unchanged by C refinement). WL55 then measures the K-side loss directly (outgoing +10 to +22 %, incident up to +5 %). The WL53 sentence 'not from K' does not hold for medium-to-medium links.

contradictions.between: WL54 addendum vs WL55 Stage B
contradictions.description: WL54 calls the gap8 oblique lower-side group 'a real transport under-prediction ... presumably on the K side' and 'not a pixel-size effect' (+0.6 % from 0.5 to 0.25 mm). WL55 attributes it to the camera readout omitting unscattered light (continuous oracle -33.5 % -> -1.7 % with the ballistic term) and finds the reference not converged (+1.2 % to 0.25 mm, then +5.0 % to 0.125 mm).

contradictions.between: WL54 Stage E vs WL55 interpretation table
contradictions.description: WL54: the bend90 slab underside blue (+4.2 % with CASP) 'is not a C-resolution effect', cause not isolated. WL55: it is an interface-spatial K-side effect (+2.3 % -> +0.5 % with matched refinement) and WL54's value was measured against WL53's 1 mm reference.

contradictions.between: WL54 headline count vs WL55 replay
contradictions.description: WL54 reports '35 of 36 ruled Lambert groups pass'. WL55's exact replay notes that at the 0.5 mm references CASP fails 2 of 36 genuine groups; the 35/36 count substitutes the 0.25 mm reference for gap4 gapdown (disclosed in WL54 A1 / A3).

contradictions.between: WL53 worklog wording vs WL53 code
contradictions.description: WL53 summarises the dent's K change as local, '91-100 % of its energy within the dent support'. In p53_oracle.py the support is r < 2 cm + 3*L_d; for red (L_d 18.1 mm) this covers every port centre of the 10 x 10 cm slab, so the red 1.00 carries no locality information. Only green (0.98) and blue (0.91) are informative.

contradictions.between: WL53 spectral-radius values vs WL54 A2 vs WL55 audit
contradictions.description: WL53's estimator is invalid for +/- eigenvalue pairs; WL54 finds it 2-4x low on refined operators and 3.6 % low on the floor-scene blue channel while gap rho values are correct; WL55 finds it within 0.02 % on the two cases it checked. WL53's convergence statements do not depend on it. WL52's lc_trace.spectral_radius is the same norm-ratio style and was never audited (its 280/280 convergence count is independent of rho).

contradictions.between: WL52 report.json vs WL52 worklog
contradictions.description: The stored criteria block records P4 with the GPU-contended benchmark (C-path 1.13x, frame 0.82x); the worklog designates the fully idle rerun as primary (0.18x / 0.31x). Both fail the predeclared rule (>= 2x and frame faster), but the number in the result JSON is not the one the verdict text uses.

contradictions.between: WL55 vs WL56 vs WL53 oracle timings
contradictions.description: The same 125.8 M-photon 2.5 mm slab operator costs 380 s in WL55 (5 camera directions, partly contended) and 175-179 s in WL56 (3 directions, idle). The 7.9 M-photon 1 cm operator costs 70 s in WL53 (4 directions, dense accumulators, GPU shared with WL52) and 22.5 s in WL55. Per-photon cost therefore differs by 2-3x between batches for reasons that were not separated.

contradictions.between: WL52 conclusion 'K dominates, C is not a meaningful cost' vs WL55 / WL56 cost splits
contradictions.description: Not a numerical conflict but two different quantities: WL52 measured per-iteration application of the K44 neural kernel (787 ms vs 23 ms for C). In the oracle pipeline per-iteration K + C is 1-4 ms and the expensive item is constructing K for a changed geometry (175-380 s). 'K is expensive' refers to application in one pipeline and to construction in the other.

contradictions.between: WL55 Stage D coded tests vs CAK 'physical correctness' verdict
contradictions.description: Two coded operator tests failed (albedo-1 closure by 1/2048 from 4 leaked photons; rigid pose ratio 1.11 / 1.12 / 1.18 outside [0.85, 1.15]). The worklog reclassifies them post hoc (test-specification error; replicates 0.82 / 0.85 / 1.05, a low-side formal miss) and keeps CONDITIONALLY SUPPORTED.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A learned replacement of the free-space coupling update has to beat a GPU explicit update of about 5 ms at ~10k ports and 11 ms at ~40k ports (BVH + 128 gathers), with application cost 0.1-0.6 ms per iteration, on scenes of this size.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL52 bench_clean: 4.98 vs 44.0 ms and 11.1 vs 672 ms; WL54: C build 14-118 ms for 340-3,840 ports at 8192 rays per port; WL56: C 0.02-0.035 s of a 0.69-1.09 s state update.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Dense receiver x source pair evaluation, O(N*M) per geometry, is not competitive with ray-cast coupling and uses about 10x the memory at 40k ports.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL52: C1 update 44 -> 110 -> 672 ms as N*M grows; F 408 MB vs 40.5 MB; top-k pruning by unoccluded form factor failed coverage (95 % at k = 256).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A source representation that averages radiance over an area larger than about half the near-field distance loses near-contact and visibility-transition transport whether or not the operator is learned; refinement to cells <= d/2 was needed for a 3 % contract with local K.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL52: ray-traced patch transfer C0p has the same localized error as the learned C1 (p99 2.30 vs 2.32); WL54: exact-transfer coarse operator reproduces +6 to +44 %, 94 % from pairs closer than the port size; CASP c = 2 passes 35/36.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A transport operator that is linear in radiance, non-negative and row-sum bounded composes stably with a passive K; stability was not the failure mode of the learned coupling.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL52: closure 0.990-0.997, rho 0.51, 280/280 solves converged, by construction of the pi-softmax with a NULL slot.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: In-medium and free-space path families must have disjoint owners; a component that also claims the other's paths makes the composition divergent.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL53 double-claim control rho 4.75 / 2.92 / 0.83 vs 0.42-0.82 for partition arms; zero back-face hits in every later composition.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: An intrinsic medium operator expressed in material coordinates is reusable under rigid motion; what must be recomputed is the geometry-dependent state (boundary cells, coupling, incident field, solve, readout), measured at 0.69 s resident for two slabs.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL53: K difference 1.00-1.05x seed noise, composition <= 0.05 %; WL55: contact-creating move 18/18 with re-aggregation only; WL56: rigid S 9.2 s from disk cache, 0.685 s resident.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Near contact (< ~1 cm), a K/C boundary-port interface must resolve exchange below the port on both the K and the C side, at the scale of the gap and the diffusion length; refining C alone does not help a port-resolved K.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL54: CASP = C0 within 0.52 points on medium links; WL55: outgoing +10 to +22 %, incident up to +5 %, contact move +19 % at 1 cm, all <= +/- 1.8 % at 2.5 mm.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A non-rigid deformation invalidates the deformed domain's intrinsic K; keeping it stale reproduces 1-20 % of the stationary receiver's change amplitude. The change cannot be assumed local or low-rank in general.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL56: stale slope 0.199 / 0.077 / 0.0098 vs 0.975-1.040; WL53: dent rank90 8-18 and local, bend90 rank90 133-151 and dense, area-only correspondence explains < 0.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The component with a measured large cost is construction of the intrinsic K for a changed domain: 175-380 s and 1.7-2.0 GB per 10 x 10 x 1 cm slab at 2.5 mm, 92.9 % of a selective update. Photon count grows x4 per halving of the cell size and x4 for 8x8 incoming bins.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL55 cost.json (7.9 M / 31.5 M / 125.8 M photons, 22.5 / 78.3 / 380 s); WL56 dent_S runs (175.5 s TR of 188.9 s).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Whole-domain selection gives no benefit once per-domain K cost is small: under the compact resident model a >= 20 % saving needs k >= ~0.23 s, and at k = 1-10 ms selection yields 1.0015-1.014x. The remaining floor is the shared state update.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL56 A1 algebra with H = 0.685 s from the rigid resident measurement; N = 2 only; H and O not measured for a compact model.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A supervision target for a geometry-dependent K has to be defined at an aggregation level where the change exceeds oracle noise: at 2048 photons per cell that is 1 cm ports or contact-adaptive cells, not 2.5 mm cell pairs.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL55 Stage E: Delta-K / noise 1.1-1.7 at 2.5 mm pairs vs 3.6-8.1 at 1 cm; WL53: 16x photons needed to pass the magnitude rule.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A medium readout toward the camera needs the unscattered term, and a binned outgoing readout is not adequate for absolute transmitted radiance.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL55: -33.5 % -> -1.7 % with the ballistic term; WL56: lower-bottom blue +10.27 % (KC + KB) vs +33.76 % (64-bin readout).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The exact oracle at 2.5 mm cells and 64/16 bins is itself outside the 3 % physical target under a broad incident field (9/12, blue +3.6 to +10.3 %); anything supervised by or compared with it inherits that floor.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL56 physical accuracy tables; identical for full and selective arms; noise controls exclude source and C sampling.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Speed claims have to be made against an efficient explicit GPU baseline on an idle machine; the production Python relation path overstates explicit-C cost by three orders of magnitude and CPU contention changes the sign of the comparison.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL52: 277 s Python path vs ms-scale GPU path; contended runs gave 1.13x / 0.82x and 2.52x at the coarsest scale vs 0.18x / 0.31x idle.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Stale-versus-updated transport cannot be ranked by absolute image error where the interface bias floor exceeds half the paired difference; signed-change slope and correlation were the usable measures.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: WL53: stale effect <= 2.3 % below the ~5 % floor; WL54: bias floor 0.5-5.5 % > |D|/2; WL55: rank met only on the bend90 underside after refinement; WL56: stale K closer to Cycles in blue through cancellation (-0.16 % vs +9.35 %).

open_confounds: Explicit-C cost at Lego scale was never measured end to end on the GPU: 0.105 s is a trace-only extrapolation from random rays, the BVH build is 0.82 s, and device-side hit-to-port mapping and an incremental GPU update for 854k ports do not exist. WL52's 5 ms figure is for scenes of ~20k triangles, where the BVH build is 2 ms.

Learned C was tested as one architecture (dense GLT), one patch size (12.5 cm), one training seed, Lambertian K, diffuse irradiance only, one synthetic scene family. Finer patches, sparse or hierarchical candidates and directional transport were not trained, so the split between 'representation loss' and 'learning loss' holds only for that configuration.

WL52's oracle is itself port-quantised (3.1 cm ports, 2048 gathers) and the coupled reference's split noise (0.09-0.11) is of the same size as the arm errors it ranks (0.11-0.16). The localized-error metric that carries the P2 verdict was defined post hoc.

Intrinsic-K cost scaling is known for one domain size and one medium (10 x 10 x 1 cm, sigma_t 1000 /m, albedo 0.999 / 0.99 / 0.9, isotropic, index-matched). Dependence on domain volume, optical thickness, albedo (collisions per photon), heterogeneity and refraction was not measured; per-photon throughput varied 0.11-0.72 M photons/s across batches with camera-direction count, accumulator type and contention confounded.

Rigid invariance of K is bounded only by Monte Carlo noise (~0.9 % relative Frobenius at 2048 photons per cell, one rotation, port-pair level). WL55's coded rigid test formally missed its band. WL56's rigid control is identity by construction (same canonical mesh and seeds), not an independent physical test, and covers a translation only.

Non-rigid Delta-K structure was measured on direction-summed port-pair matrices at 1 cm for one dent and two bends; rank90 depends on the noise level (dent 65-91 at 2048 photons, 8-18 at 32768), the red locality figure is vacuous, and directional structure of the change is indistinguishable from noise at 2.5 mm.

The blue residual of the exact oracle (+3.6 to +10.3 %) has no attributed cause; WL55's validation used an exact first-order sun term and did not exercise a broad incident field passing entirely through K.

Selective-update cost was measured for N = 2 domains with 0 or 1 dirty, a whole-domain unit, warm page cache and a 1.68 GB package with 3.3 s hashing each. Runs without TR show higher shared times (1.4-1.5 s vs 1.07-1.09 s), consistent with a cold-GPU effect that was not isolated. N = 4 / 8 values are algebraic projections.

Oblique and through-gap groups in WL53-55 are reference-limited: point-sampled Cycles pixels are not converged at 0.125 mm, so CAK's oblique failures and the held-out gap6s residual cannot be cleanly separated into reference and interface parts.

CAK's tractability failure is relative to the uniform 2.5 mm arm with the single level rule c = 2; no stricter rule and no sub-2.5 mm oracle were tested. The 2.5 mm oracle is treated as converged on the basis of face-on groups only.
Cycles CUDA (official 3.5.1 build) vs the CPU fork is inherited from the user's validation in WL55 / WL56 and was not re-checked; WL53's physical-validity results were obtained on the CPU.

All fixtures are index-matched, isotropic and homogeneous with voxel geometry; refraction, anisotropic phase functions, self-contact and connectivity changes are untested, and WL47's direction-selective regime is outside this scope.

WL52's 'K is 95 % of a step' is one view of one pipeline with the K44 kernel; it does not transfer to other K representations, where the per-iteration cost is milliseconds and the cost sits in per-geometry construction.
narrative_summary:
WL52 trained one geometry-conditioned learned coupling (GLT: patch-token transformer, dense receiver x patch transfer, pi-softmax with a NULL slot). The operator is linear, non-negative and passive by construction, converged in 280/280 coupled solves (rho 0.51) and did not memorise. It lost on two measured points. Cost: on an idle RTX 3090 the explicit update (BVH + 128 gathers) took 5.0 ms at ~10k ports and 11.1 ms at ~40k, against 44.0 and 672 ms for the learned update; application cost was equal (0.1-0.6 ms). Information: near-contact and visibility-transition errors were 8-9x those of explicit C, and the ray-traced transfer on the same 12.5 cm patch representation was almost as bad, so the loss sits mainly in the area-averaged source representation. The Lego-scale explicit figure (0.105 s) is a trace-only extrapolation, not an end-to-end measurement.

WL53 established Cycles volume path tracing as a path-history-independent reference and defined the intrinsic K as entry-to-first-exit transport of an isolated medium domain. The oracle matched the reference within 0.4 % on main faces, K was invariant under a rigid rotation within Monte Carlo noise, and double-claiming paths between K and C diverged (rho 4.75). Non-rigid deformation changed K by 0.5-1.9 % (port-pair Frobenius): low-rank for a dent, dense for a bend.

WL54 showed that with an exact local K the 1 cm coupling error (+6 to +44 %) is convex sub-port source structure from pairs closer than a port; contact-adaptive sub-port coupling brought 35/36 groups within 3 % at 1.00-1.04x GPU work. It had no effect on a port-resolved medium K.

WL55 measured the K-side loss directly (outgoing flux +10 to +22 %, incident up to +5 % at 1 cm, convergent at 2.5 mm), attributed an earlier oblique error to a missing ballistic readout term, and showed that a 2.5 mm material-coordinate operator re-aggregated to contact-adaptive cells handles a contact-creating rigid move without new tracing (18/18 vs 12/18). The 2.5 mm oracle costs 126 M photons, 380 s and 2.0 GB per slab; photons grow x4 per halving of cell size.

WL56 showed exact whole-domain selective recomputation equals full recomputation (relative L1 1.55e-8) at 188.9 s versus 371.4 s. Of the selective update, 175.5 s (92.9 %) is tracing the changed domain's K; all current-state work (boundary, coupling 0.03 s, incident field, solve, readout) is about 1.1 s, and 0.685 s with K resident. A stale K recovered 1-20 % of the stationary receiver's change. The oracle itself passes only 9/12 face-on channel tests (blue +3.6 to +10.3 %).

Several earlier interpretations were revised by later batches (WL53's "C only" attribution, WL54's oblique-group and bend90 readings). Cost scaling of K with domain size, optical density or heterogeneity, explicit-C cost at Lego scale, and any learned K were not measured in this scope.

implementation_facts.claim: Compiler inputs (the only conditioning): alpha_i (coat roughness, [0.05, 0.5] log), eta (coat IOR, [1.3, 1.8]), tau (slab optical thickness, [0.02, 2.0] log), a_rgb (slab single-scattering albedo, [0, 0.99]), r_rgb (conductor reflectance, [0.05, 0.98]), alpha_b (base roughness, [0.05, 0.6] log). A joint block alpha_i [0.05,0.1] x tau [0.5,2] x alpha_b [0.3,0.6] (~2.5 % of the box) is excluded from training and used as test_block.

The reference the closure approximates is one material family: a rough dielectric coat over a homogeneous isotropic-scattering slab over a rough GGX conductor, evaluated by a position-free random walk (port of pbrt-v4 LayeredBxDF with one MIS correction, max depth 1024). Position-free means the reference itself has no lateral displacement; it is an opaque, isotropic, pointwise BSDF.

Populations: train83 = 3000 and val83 = 200 WL81 materials; new evaluation draws test83_iid 300 (outside the block), test83_block 200 (inside the held-out block), test83_hard 150 (tau in [0.02, 0.0928], alpha_b in [0.05, 0.1145], mean conductor reflectance >= 0.582); real83 = 8 parameterised named finishes, not measured BRDFs. Response data 64 wi x 64 wo x 1024 walks per material.

A float32 refraction defect (t_z cancels to 0 near the horizon when eta_e -> 1) is fixed by the algebraically identical form t_z = sqrt(max(eta^2-1,0) + w_z^2)/eta, monkey-patched into closure82 by closure83.install() and native in the Dr.Jit runtime; compiler training, evaluation and the WL85 census all import the patch.

The census and the WL85 references use only the seed-8301 learned ER closures (fit_<set>_L_ER_s8301.npz).

WL84A produced no code, training, rendering or measurement: 3 sealed design tracks, 4 adversarial reviews, 3 novelty searches, 3 cross-reviews, 1 provenance audit, coordinator synthesis (14 agents, ~33 min).

Track A (DDT / DDT-D): persist a 4D outgoing radiance field b0(x, omega_o) on all surfaces; after a rigid edit enumerate changed rays through the mover's old/new pose, evaluate the first-order source from two b0 lookups per ray, propagate magnitude through K C1 to a tolerance, overwrite the marked cells by regather. Identity (I - K C1) db = K(de + dC b0).

Track B (ERPS): store sampled paths (vertices, random numbers, lobe choice, contribution); after the edit test every stored segment against the mover's old and new placement; keep clean paths bit-identically, replay dirty suffixes (PR1), or use a T0 image + difference paths (PR2), or reservoirs with GRIS temporal reuse (PR3). No learned state beyond the 69-float ER states.

Track C (LPTG): split each material's ER lobes at a roughness threshold alpha* into rough set R and sharp set S; persist indirect incident radiance I(c, j) at N cache points on K fixed material-frame directions; apply R events through a per-material K x K matrix B compiled from ER; carry S events as stored replayable ray chains (fresh chains at camera readout); certify stored segments geometrically after the edit, regenerate invalid chains, re-solve the field warm-started. It adds no learned parameters above ER.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL81's representation failure was mainly an incidence-independent energy limitation (H1); refraction-aware angular shape (H2) is not necessary for the population target but is what reduces the remaining error in thin / sharp / high-reflectance materials.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Direct-fit errors of four closure arms on 300 held-out materials (E_cert passes the WL81 gate, C0 fails; ER_cert 0.052 vs E_cert 0.073; cluster 0.109 vs 0.184, n = 10). No ablation isolates 'refraction' from 'one extra angular degree of freedom'; fitted eta_e does not correlate with the true IOR.

worklog_interpretations.claim: ER's gain is 'a useful refraction-shaped angular degree of freedom, not evidence that the representation learned the coat's refraction'.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: eta_e vs eta correlation -0.20..+0.14, values at the range limits 1.0 / 2.5.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The learned-compiler question is answered positively for this family: descriptor-to-closure compilation generalises with a small transfer cost.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Learned vs direct-fit E_L1 on 300 + 150 + 200 new synthetic materials of the SAME parametric family, two seeds (0.057 vs 0.053 iid; block 0.067 vs 0.053). No measured BRDF, no material outside the 10-parameter coated-conductor box.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The certificate is conservative (cert gap = price of the sum-lambda <= 1 sufficient condition).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: cert vs unbounded fit error (E 0.073 vs 0.043; ER 0.052 vs 0.038) and an empirical sampler audit in which fitted unbounded closures stayed <= 1 at audited directions. No tighter certificate was attempted.

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL83's sole ER_L rendering failure was a reference-qualification artefact, not a scattering deficiency.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: With a 16x reference (uncertainty 0.0066 instead of 0.0265) ER_L's highlight error on that image is 0.093 vs gate 0.10, 8/8 replicate seeds pass. The margin is 0.007; only 3 of 10 WL83 images were re-qualified.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The closures have a bias floor of about 0.035-0.04 image L1; beyond ~1024 spp the layered reference is more accurate per unit GPU time.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: ER_L error at 1024 spp (0.0425 / 0.0347 / 0.0378) on one ladder per image, still decreasing from 256 spp (0.060 / 0.051 / 0.053); no higher-spp ER point and no noise/bias split. The value is an upper bound on the asymptotic bias on 3 object-only images, not a measured asymptote.

worklog_interpretations.claim: ER's local-rendering cost advantage is real in GPU execution and moderate (~1.5x per spp), limited to quality levels above its bias floor, and does not reach wall time in this harness.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Kernel GPU time per 64 spp (REF/ER 1.45-1.63) and equal wall time (Python tracing 85-95 %) on 3 images at 256^2, depth 4. No production-runtime measurement.

worklog_interpretations.claim: All three WL84A tracks are indefensible as the GM1 global mechanism; recommendation class C with D (no candidate defensible; missing evidence first).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing. Design-only: derivations and order-of-magnitude estimates (labelled DERIV / EST), agent agreement. The coordinator itself states a factor of 3 in constants can open or close a window and that the review does not show no defensible mechanism exists.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Track A's advocate withdrew it because (i) a tabulated 4D outgoing state scales as alpha^-4 (~38 GB at alpha = 0.05 for a 5 m^2 court), (ii) the dirty fraction needed for single-view break-even (5e-4 to 8e-3) is below its geometric lower bound (~3 %), (iii) the band-limited + continuation variant is either LPTG or residual path tracing (Xu et al. 2024), (iv) every bounce passes through the state (5 % peak loss per lookup), (v) no novelty; what survives is a solver policy (HYP-delta) on someone else's state, predicted by its own advocate to fail at K = 128, rho ~0.8.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; derivations from 21_ (N_omega ~ 16/alpha^2, spatial spacing d*0.64*alpha) and 22_ (cost model with assumed unit costs c_path 2.4 ns derived from WL84, c_touch 0.15-0.5 ns assumed).

worklog_interpretations.claim: Track B's advocate confirmed it is not a mechanism: it holds no transport representation (a retracer with sampling memory, excluded by the roadmap's GM1 exit clause), has no novelty (ReSTIR PT / GRIS, Bala et al. 1999, Guenther & Grosch 2015, Xu et al. 2024); PR3 withdrawn (T0-domain shift for mover vertices unspecified), PR2's economic claim withdrawn (wins only with an over-converged, uncharged T0 anchor), the '1/rho bound for any selective scheme' withdrawn; only the paired same-seed T0/T1 path log survives as a measurement and PR1 as a lower-bound warm comparator.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; variance algebra and the reviewers' estimates.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Track C's advocate withdrew LPTG as a GM1 mechanism for three independent accepted reasons: (1) the camera-visible sharp highlight comes from fresh per-frame chains, so the persistent state holds no sharp directional content (a retracer for the sharp part); (2) the incident field is point-sampled, not band-limited, so sharp-sender -> rough-stationary-receiver transport aliases coherently (0.16-0.64 nodes per highlight at alpha_S 0.05, K = 128) with no convergence path at fixed state size; (3) the field re-solve is dense per edit, so S ~ F in cost; plus nothing global is learned. Residual roles: admission census, REF-ER path-class instrumentation, possible learning-free physical baseline.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing; derivations in 20_ C-1/C-2, 21_ C1-C3, 22_ C1, 23_ C-1.

worklog_interpretations.claim: At ER's sharpness the only persistent directional content any reviewed design can hold at practical size is a field band-limited near alpha* ~ 0.2-0.35; angular requirement scales ~alpha^-2 and a 4D outgoing state ~alpha^-4.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Small-angle GGX derivation calibrated against one historical measurement (WL58: 256 piecewise-constant bins lose 9.9-17.7 % relative L2 at alpha 0.25, 52-80 % at alpha 0.04, static analytic GGX). alpha* estimates span a factor ~3 across reviewers (0.125 to 0.35).

worklog_interpretations.claim: Economics objection applying to any cache / reuse mechanism: cold frozen-ER path tracing is so cheap (~2.4 ns per complete depth-4 path) that a ray costs about as much as 1-5 random memory accesses; 'arithmetic on stored data instead of tracing' is an advantage only when the stored data touched is much smaller than the rays avoided; in all three designs the selective part is not the dominant cost.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Only the anchor is measured (WL84: ~10 ms GPU per 64 spp at 256^2). c_touch, c_gather and all break-evens are assumptions/derivations; the review notes a factor of 3 can open or close Track C's window.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Identifiability objections applying to any stored-state or learned-global mechanism (X1-X8): quality matching between a biased, spatially correlated estimator and unbiased white noise is undefined; quality levels must be anchored to the in-scene ER gap g before results; signed-change slope/correlation is attenuated by reference noise; arms need >= 8 replicate seeds; T0 investment (state build, converged T0 image) must be charged and a masked cold re-render control added; cost verdicts must separate mechanism from implementation maturity (work counts + kernel time); F = S hides every error F and S share.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Nothing new; based on historical patterns (WL38 seed spread 0.23 dB, WL84 reference-limited class, WL59 F/S 1e-7 with failing fidelity, WL67-70 loose contracts met at 1-16 spp).

worklog_interpretations.claim: On the WL85 fixture a GM1 mechanism would have to carry three things: exact direct visibility change; small-magnitude broad-to-broad multi-bounce change over the whole scene; a spatially local sharp/moderate-sender family that is not negligible there.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Class shares of |change| per region on one fixture/edit (direct 0.66 of stationary |change|; B<-S 0.20 of the enabled region; M<-S 0.25 on the sphere; stationary-rest change 1.5 % of T0). Formally INDETERMINATE because the frozen workload gate failed (Q3b 0.465 < 0.50).

worklog_interpretations.claim: To be useful at the ER-gap quality level a reuse mechanism would have to beat ~0.4 s of GPU work per frame with a millisecond-scale edit; the ~21 % dirty work fraction bounds what path-granular replay could skip.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Cold REF-ER ladder (387 ms GPU to reach g = 0.017 over stationary pixels at 512^2), in-place edit 2.5 ms, dirty path/segment fractions 20-23 %. The bound applies to path-granular replay with this sampler; it is not a bound on field- or link-granular reuse (23_ B-3, 42_ §2).

worklog_interpretations.claim: WL84A assumptions after WL85: A1 (meaningful Lambert/broad share for every material) WEAKENED; A2 PARTLY SUPPORTED; A3 (sharp-sender -> rough-receiver material) SUPPORTED locally; A4 (dense change support) SUPPORTED with small magnitude; A5 (dirty fraction a few to 15 %) WEAKENED (20-21 %); A6 (cold REF-ER reaches the anchored quality in about a second) SUPPORTED (0.39 s GPU); A7 (caustic-type family reference-limited) WEAKENED on this fixture; A8 (Python tracing dominates wall) SUPPORTED.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Census, class accounting and ladder on one fixture with a point light, a stationary sharp panel of closure r50 ~0.15 rad and a diffuse mover. A7's weakening does not cover a sharp MOVING sender, an area light, or alpha below ~0.05.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The WL85 failed qualification clause reflects the region definition; the target phenomenon is present.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Post hoc (labelled): 3,643 of 28,835 enabled-region pixels also have their direct light unblocked by the edit; in the remaining 25,192 pixels the change is +3.6 % of T0 with 99.4 % from >= 2 events. The sub-region was defined after seeing the failure; acceptance is left to the human owner.

worklog_interpretations.claim: No reviewed mechanism has mechanism novelty; every central mechanism is ALREADY KNOWN; what a credible contribution requires is measured quality-matched lifecycle utility for a mechanism that holds learned global state.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Bounded literature searches (20 of 23 spot-checked citations VERIFIED, 2 PARTLY, 1 UNVERIFIED); 'no published instance found' statements are weak negatives.

contradictions.between: WL83 verdict (OUTCOME D, RENDER fail) vs WL84 verdict (OUTCOME A)
contradictions.description: Same closures, same stored 64-spp candidates. WL83 failed the all-images rendering rule (ER_L 9/10, the failing image reference-limited at 4096 spp); WL84 passes ER_L on the 3 re-qualified images with a 65,536-spp reference. WL83 OUTCOME D is kept as the historical verdict; the other 7 images were not re-qualified and their time-matched comparisons used contended GPU timing.

contradictions.between: WL84 worklog label 'bias floor ~0.035-0.04' vs econ84.json curves
contradictions.description: The curve is still falling at the last ER point (0.060 -> 0.0425, 0.051 -> 0.0347, 0.053 -> 0.0378 from 256 to 1024 spp) and there is one ladder per image. The quoted floor is the 1024-spp error (noise + bias), i.e. an upper bound on the bias, not a measured asymptote. WL85's noise-free in-scene gap (65,536 spp pooled) is region-dependent: 0.017 stationary, 0.056 enabled region, 0.069 sharp panel.

contradictions.between: WL84A coordinator synthesis §5 (falsification clause) vs WL85 measurement
contradictions.description: 60_ states: if cold REF-ER reaches the ER-gap-anchored quality in about a second or less on the GM1 fixture, no reuse scheme of any track has economic room on that workload. WL85 measured 0.39 s GPU (2.06 s wall) to reach g. WL85 nonetheless records its architecture conclusions as formally INDETERMINATE because the workload gate failed one clause, so the clause is triggered by a measurement that the frozen rule says may not be used for conclusions.

contradictions.between: WL84A reviews (21_ A3, 40_ §2, 42_ §3.1: 'every ER material has a Lambert lobe', labelled FACT) vs WL85 census
contradictions.description: The closure has a Lambert SLOT; its fitted weight is small on the hard population (median share 0.04, only 7 % of materials >= 10 %) and moderate on iid (median 0.20). The provenance audit (50_ §2.2) had already flagged the label. The argument that residual support is dense after one rough bounce rested on this; WL85 nevertheless measured that change reaches nearly all stationary pixels through broad paths (stationary-rest |change| 1.5 % of T0, B<-B 0.60) on a fixture whose floor is 99.8 % broad.

contradictions.between: WL84A economics estimates vs WL85 measurements of path structure
contradictions.description: 22_ assumed ~8 segments per depth-4 path and a per-segment dirty probability ~2 % (15 % dirty paths) for a small mover; WL85 measured 2.36-2.42 segments per path and 20-21 % dirty paths (21-23 % dirty segment work) for a 0.7 m baffle crossing the light beam in an open scene. The measured fixture is neither the 'small mover in a closed room' of the estimates nor a closed glossy court.

contradictions.between: WL84A (21_ §1.5, 60_ §2.2: the headline caustic-type class is noise-limited even at 65,536 spp) vs WL85 (A7 weakened)
contradictions.description: WL85 found the enabled-region reference well resolved (uncertainty 0.006 vs change 0.105). Conditions differ from the estimate: point light with next-event estimation through the sender lobe, stationary panel with closure r50 ~0.15 rad (alpha ~0.07, 43 % sharp), diffuse mover. The estimate (hit rate alpha^2-4 alpha^2 for a small light and a sharp sender at alpha 0.05 or below) is neither confirmed nor refuted for sharper or moving senders.

contradictions.between: WL85 class thresholds vs WL84A alpha* band
contradictions.description: WL85's broad class starts at r50 0.45 rad (alpha ~0.22) and its sharp class ends at r50 0.15 (alpha ~0.075). WL84A's band-limit for a practical persistent field is alpha* 0.17-0.35 (r50 ~0.34-0.7). The 'moderate' class (r50 0.15-0.45), which holds a median 94 % of the hard population's albedo and 41 % of iid, therefore lies mostly BELOW alpha* and would be traced, not stored, under the WL84A rule. WL85's label 'A2 partly supported' uses the 0.45 boundary only.

contradictions.between: WL83 'ER worth' gate vs compute-bound cost
contradictions.description: The frozen rule uses the memory-bound io ratio (ER/E eval_pdf 1.05 <= 1.5) and passes; in the compute-bound fused16 regime ER/E is ~1.64 (ER 17.1 ms vs E 10.5 ms; 3.62x C0), which exceeds the 1.5 limit. Both are reported; the verdict depends on which regime represents a renderer.

contradictions.between: REF/ER in-renderer cost ratio, WL84 vs WL85
contradictions.description: WL84: 1.45-1.63x per spp (Mitsuba path + plugin, 256^2, depth 4, one ER object). WL85: REF-P 2.86x REF-ER (pt85, 512^2, depth 6, three ER objects, one-walk layered eval). Not inconsistent, but 'about 1.5x' in the WL84A brief is specific to the WL84 scene.

contradictions.between: WL84A cross-reviews 41_ vs 42_ (strongest competitor)
contradictions.description: 42_ names Track B 'in its PR2 / residual form' as the strongest competitor; 41_ withdraws PR2 as an economic claim and states a residual-path-integral sampler is 'not designed here'. Also unresolved: whether link-granular reuse has more headroom than path-granular (42_ yes; 41_ D3 no), and alpha* at K = 128 (0.125 to 0.35).

contradictions.between: 22_ A4 ('GM1's valid output is images at given cameras', labelled FACT) vs the roadmap text
contradictions.description: The provenance audit (50_ row 51) finds the GM1 row names no camera count; the statement is an inference. It decides whether multi-view / multi-frame workloads (the only economic windows found for stored states) are inside GM1 - an open human decision.

contradictions.between: WL82 mechanism name ('refraction-conditioned') vs fitted behaviour
contradictions.description: eta_e does not track the physical coat IOR and collapses to ~1 on the block set; the compiler receives eta as an input but nothing ties eta_e to it. The ER gain is real in error terms; its physical reading is not supported.

contradictions.between: WL85 protocol regions vs results
contradictions.description: The predeclared region 'reflection_static' contains 0 pixels in analysis.json and the predeclared 'enabled_reflection' region mixes 12.6 % pixels whose direct light is also unblocked; neither is discussed as a protocol defect in the worklog beyond the post hoc Q3b diagnostic.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: ER is a local, opaque, reflection-only BRDF surrogate for one 10-parameter coated-conductor family. Any transmission, subsurface / lateral (nonlocal K) or spatially varying material response must be carried by something else; none of WL82-85 tests it.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: closure82.py eval validity (upper hemisphere only, no position argument); compiled81.json reference physics (position-free walk, conductor base); WL83/84 scope statements ('FNTO integration NOT TESTED').

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A global mechanism evaluated against the physical reference cannot be shown more accurate than ER's own in-scene gap: 0.017 over stationary pixels, 0.056 in the reflected patch, 0.069 on the sharp panel (WL85), with ER overestimating mean change by 9-17 % in those regions. Global-mechanism error must be measured against REF-ER and judged at levels anchored to g.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: analysis.json gap_T1 / change_ER_vs_P; 23_ X2 (anchoring rule).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: ER's error is concentrated at grazing incidence (E_L1 median 0.076-0.097 at 80-86 deg vs 0.045-0.05 near normal; p90 0.16-0.19) and in thin-slab / sharp-coat / high-reflectance materials (hard-set median ~0.10). A mechanism whose evidence relies on grazing interreflection or on the hard family inherits a larger local bias.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: eval83_test83_iid.json E_L1_by_theta, strata; WL83 hard-set table; eval84.json gz_err (0.11-0.25, noise-confounded).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The comparator any cache / reuse / learned-global mechanism must beat on a WL85-scale workload is cold path tracing with frozen ER: 0.73 ms GPU per spp at 512^2, 387 ms GPU to reach the ER-gap level, 1.17 s to reach 1 % error, with a 2.5 ms in-place edit and no state. A mechanism's total edit-to-valid-output work (build amortisation, discovery, update, readout) has to fit under that, or the workload has to be larger.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: econ85.json budget / ladder_median; posthoc85.json edits_in_place.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Path-granular replay can skip at most ~77-79 % of segment work on this edit (dirty segment work 21-23 %), i.e. a ceiling of roughly 4-5x before store-read and bookkeeping costs.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: analysis.json refs.ER.segment_dirty_fraction; 22_ §3.2 ceiling formula 1/(rho + c_touch/c_path) (derivation).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Angular content is not uniformly broad: on the hard population a median 94 % of albedo is in lobes with r50 0.15-0.45 rad and only 4 % in broad lobes; sharp share rises strongly toward grazing (median 0.51 at 80 deg on iid). A persistent directional state band-limited at r50 ~0.4-0.7 would own about half the reflected energy on the iid family and a few per cent on the hard family at 45 deg, less at grazing.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: census.json theta_45 / theta_80; alpha* band from 21_ (derivation).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Tabulating outgoing radiance at ER's sharpness is infeasible at practical size: angular samples ~16/alpha^2 per point and spatial spacing ~d*0.64*alpha give a 4D count ~alpha^-4/d_min^2. This is a property of explicit tabulation with a fixed basis; the review did not examine a learned state whose angular content is conditioned on geometry.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: 21_ §1.3-1.4, A1 (derivation calibrated on WL58: 256 bins lose 10-18 % at alpha 0.25, 52-80 % at alpha 0.04); coordinator reservation in 60_ §3.

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Band-limiting the material's lobes does not band-limit the incident field: a fixed-direction K-node incident-radiance store aliases sharp senders and small occluders onto rough receivers (0.16-0.64 nodes per highlight at alpha 0.05, K = 128; a 0.2 m face at 1.15 m seen by 0.6 nodes). Any point-sampled incident-field state needs prefiltering or enough nodes to resolve the sender, not the receiver lobe.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: 20_ C-1, 21_ C1 / C3, 41_ D1 (derivations, unmeasured).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: The edit response on stationary receivers has three components with different carriers: direct visibility change (66-70 % of stationary |change|), a spatially dense but small broad multi-bounce change (stationary-rest |change| 1.5 % of T0, comparable to g), and a local sharp/moderate-sender family (B<-S 0.20 and B<-M 0.28 of the enabled-region |change|; M<-S 0.25 on the sphere). A mechanism that reproduces only the frame-level (0.82 all-broad) share would miss the regions that define the phenomenon.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: analysis.json class accounting; WL85 worklog (formally INDETERMINATE under the frozen gate).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A same-architecture F = S equality is an implementation test only; it cannot detect any discretisation, aliasing or frozen-sample error the two share. Fidelity claims need independent-seed replicates (>= 8), bias/variance split, multi-scale matching, and both lifecycle (T0 + T1) and edit-to-output accounting; signed-change slopes need a reference-noise model.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: 23_ X1-X6, C-2; 20_ §5 item 2 (derivations; historical precedents WL59, WL38, WL84).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: A result from a mechanism with no learned global state cannot be reported as selective recompute of learned transport; under current central documents it is unclear whether a learning-free global solve around frozen ER is admissible as candidate or baseline only (open human decision).
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: 23_ X7; 50_ §5.4; 35_ last paragraph; Track C §2 ('adds no learned parameters').

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Central mechanisms of all three reviewed classes are published: incremental (glossy) radiosity and delta transfer (Chen 1990; Drettakis & Sillion 1997; Granier & Drettakis 2001; Loos et al. 2012), stored-ray invalidation (Bala et al. 1999), residual / difference re-rendering (Guenther & Grosch 2015; Rousselle et al. 2016; Xu et al. 2024), reservoir reuse (ReSTIR GI / GRIS / ReSTIR PT), two-pass rough/sharp partition and radiance caching (Sillion et al. 1991; NRC 2021), learned 4D radiance states (Neural Radiosity 2021; dynamic neural radiosity 2024), per-object neural transfer composed at runtime (NeLT 2023; TransGI 2025), learned cache as control variate (Neural Control Variates 2020). Novelty cannot rest on these; warm path-traced re-rendering (Xu et al. 2024, ReSTIR PT) and online caches (NRC-class) are comparators a reviewer would ask for and are unmeasured in the project.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: 35_prior_art_matrix.md; 30_ §3; 32_ §3; 50_ §4 (20/23 citations verified at search level).

constraints_for_future_architecture.constraint: Cost evidence must use kernel GPU time or work counts: in the Dr.Jit 0.4.6 harness Python tracing is 70-95 % of wall time (0.18 s per 64 spp in WL85, 0.4-1.2 s per launch in WL84), so wall-clock differences below ~1 s are not attributable to a mechanism.
constraints_for_future_architecture.basis: econ84.json trace_s; econ85.json; 22_ §1.2 consequence 3; 23_ X6.

open_confounds: ER generality: trained and validated only on synthetic draws from one 10-parameter coated-conductor box (plus 8 parameterised 'finishes' that are not measured BRDFs); no measured material, no other family.
The asymptotic image-space bias of ER is not measured: WL84's '0.035-0.043' is the 1024-spp error on one ladder per image (3 images, object pixels only) and still contains Monte Carlo noise.
WL84 re-qualified only 3 of the 10 WL83 images; the other 7 rest on 4096-spp references and GPU timings taken under 5 concurrent processes.

ER's fidelity in multi-bounce glossy chains was qualified only indirectly: WL84 used depth 4 with limited indirect light; WL85 measures a region-mean gap in one open, direct-light-dominated scene (84.7 % of stationary radiance is one-event; 2.4 segments per path). A closed, high-albedo glossy enclosure is unmeasured for both g and cost.

WL85's architecture-relevant readings are formally INDETERMINATE under its frozen rule (Q3b 0.465 < 0.50); the supporting sub-region diagnostic is post hoc and its acceptance is an undecided human question.

WL85 class shares depend on the declared r50 thresholds (0.15 / 0.45 rad), on class assignment at 45 deg incidence only (lobes narrow toward grazing), and on three specific materials; the sharpest closure exercised has r50 ~0.15 rad (alpha ~0.07) although the closure permits alpha down to 0.004.

The WL85 mover is a diffuse occluder and the light is a point light sampled by next-event estimation; a sharp moving sender, an area light, continuous motion and other edit types are untested, so the 'reference-limited caustic class' estimate of WL84A is neither confirmed nor refuted for those cases.

All WL84A cost and fidelity conclusions rest on unmeasured unit constants (c_touch, c_gather, 'half the dirty path'), small-angle single-lobe derivations and a three-track design space; alpha* estimates differ by a factor ~3; a factor of 3 in constants can open or close Track C's window (stated by the reviewers and the coordinator).

The dense-residual argument against an output-sensitive solve (40_ §2, 42_) assumed a Lambert weight a_L ~0.5; the census shows 0.04 (hard) to 0.20 (iid) median, 0.50 only on the block set. Whether a thresholded residual is small and safe was never measured.
No warm path-traced comparator (residual path integrals, ReSTIR PT, masked cold re-render), denoised path tracing or online radiance cache was measured; only cold REF-ER and Mitsuba's megakernel.

Wall-clock economics under a production runtime (frozen functions / megakernel / C++ BSDF) are unmeasured in WL83-85; all wall numbers are dominated by Dr.Jit Python tracing, and kernel-cache misses cost ~36 s.

ER vs E selection: ER's advantage is concentrated in the hard family (0.10 vs 0.19) and one hard-material highlight; in compute-bound kernels ER costs ~1.64x E, and eta_e is not physically identified. Census and WL85 used only the seed-8301 ER closures.

The WL83 sampler / pdf consistency tests under uniform quadrature were restricted to lobes with alpha >= 0.1 in test closures; evidence for sampling correctness of sharper lobes is indirect (sample-pdf consistency over 235,526 samples, passivity audit, highlight images).
The per-pixel distribution of the small broad change in WL85 (fraction of pixels above a threshold) was not tabulated; region means may hide localised structure.

posthoc85.json records a non-empty 'foreign' GPU process list (PID 1975265) for the post-chain in-place-edit timing; whether it is the script's own process was not checked, so those post hoc timings are not certified uncontended (the frozen econ85.json has empty foreign_before / foreign_after).
narrative_summary:
The learned ER closure is a per-material, pointwise reflection model: one Lambert lobe plus seven anisotropic GGX lobes, a symmetric incident/outgoing attenuation on the inner group (five knots per colour channel) and one fitted scalar that evaluates the four inner GGX lobes at coat-refracted directions. It has 64 raw parameters and a 69-float runtime state, is passive and reciprocal by construction, and is produced by a 150,848-parameter MLP from a 10-float descriptor of a coated-conductor material (coat roughness and index, slab thickness and albedo, base reflectance and roughness). It was trained on 3,000 synthetic materials of that one family and validated on 650 new ones. Code confirms it contains no transmission, no lateral or subsurface transport and no spatial dependence.

Measured bias: median energy-weighted relative L1 of 0.057 on the independent population, about 0.10 on thin, sharp, high-reflectance materials, and rising with incidence angle to 0.076–0.097 at 80–86 degrees. In images its error at 1024 samples per pixel was 0.035–0.043 on three images; that figure is an upper bound on its bias, not a measured asymptote. In the WL85 scene the noise-free gap to the physical reference is 0.017 over stationary pixels, 0.056 in the reflected patch and 0.069 on the sharp panel.

Cost: against a quality-matched layered reference the operator is 44 to 10,600 times cheaper, but inside a path tracer the gain is 1.45–1.63 times per sample (WL84) and 2.9 times in the WL85 fixture; no wall-clock gain exists in the Python-traced harness.

WL84A was design-only. All three candidate mechanisms were withdrawn by their own advocates: the directional delta state because a tabulated outgoing field scales as the inverse fourth power of roughness and its break-even dirty fraction lies below a geometric lower bound; path reuse because it holds no representation and is published; the lobe-partitioned graph because its sharp part is retraced, its point-sampled field aliases sharp senders onto rough receivers, and its per-edit solve is dense. Nothing global was learned in any of them. The economics and identifiability reviews raise objections that apply to any stored-state mechanism, but rest on estimates.

WL85 measured the two numbers the review lacked. The fitted closures are about half broad on the general population and 94 % moderate on the hard one, sharpening toward grazing. On one fixture with a diffuse mover, 20–21 % of paths are dirty; direct light carries 66–70 % of the stationary change; sharp or moderate senders matter locally. Cold path tracing reaches the ER-gap quality in 0.39 s of GPU time with a 2.5 ms edit. The workload failed one predeclared qualification clause, so these readings are formally indeterminate.

implementation_facts.claim: Geometry state: 512 rays per patch (8 per incident bin, same stratified offsets for every patch, table_seed 86001) storing hit patch (-1 for miss or back face), outgoing bin at the hit patch, and the segment. Selective update re-traces rays whose segment crosses the old or new OBB of a moved box (1 mm pad) or that start on the moved box.

Generator inputs are geometry only: per patch centroid x 0.5, normal, tangent, log area, an MLP of the frozen 69-d ER state of the patch material, and openness (1 - row sum of the form-factor matrix); 3 rounds of message passing over the dense N x N form-factor matrix built from the state rays plus a global mean; softplus heads give c, a [N, 64, 3, 16], Q [N, 3, 24, 16], P [N, 3, 16, 24]. The generator never receives s, light positions or radiance. 735,664 parameters.

Operator application: u = c.s; Bq = a.u (the operator's own estimate of once-scattered sender radiance, never supervised separately); E1[n, bin] = sum over the 8 state rays of that bin of Bq[hit, dbin] x cos dOmega / 8 (the single learned flight, current visibility); y = c.E1 + P.(sum_n area_n Q_n u_n); B = a.y. Only einsums with softplus factors, non-negative ray weights and areas: linear in s, zero in -> zero out, non-negative. RGB channels are processed independently (no cross-channel term). No row-sum / passivity constraint.

The same per-patch factors c and a serve three roles (direct source -> sender radiance, flight irradiance -> activation, activation -> output radiance), so the local bin-to-bin scattering of every patch, including the sharp panel, passes through R = 16 non-negative channels per colour for 64 incident and 64 outgoing bins.

implementation_facts.claim: The global term has no pairwise visibility at application time: geometry enters it only through the generated per-patch P and Q tables (tokens that saw form-factor messages) and the patch area; it is a rank-24 mixing per colour.

Loss: squared error divided by (target patch mean over bins + 5 % of the lighting's field mean), averaged with equal weight over all patch x bin x RGB entries (no area, camera-importance or mirror-readout weighting). Adam, lr 1e-3 cosine to 1e-5, 500 warm-up steps, gradient clip 10, one geometry (4 lightings) per step, 24,000 steps (each of the 1,024 geometries is visited about 23 times).

Not at noise for class E of E1 (0.025 vs 0.008) and the sphere (0.0105 vs 0.0059). One patch and bin resolution, one camera, point lights.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The learned operator works on unseen poses and lights of the family for broad transport; the field-level evidence does not show memorisation.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Aggregate validation / training-subset relative L1 ratio 1.12-1.13 (noise-inflated), debiased RMS ratio 1.17-1.23; stationary and D-region E_H 0.003-0.006 on E1 and E2. WL86A's per-class numbers on the same checkpoints show 1.6-2.7x larger error on unseen box patches and 1.3-2.5x on panel-facing broad patches (debiased RMS).

worklog_interpretations.claim: Both learned terms are needed.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Switching off one term of the jointly trained model raises stationary E_H to 0.11-0.13 (each term carries about half of the higher-order radiance). No model was trained with only one term.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The sharp-receiver error is the learned operator's (3-5x the oracle), not the representation's.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Panel object E_H 0.034-0.056 for the learned table against 0.012 for the oracle table with identical readout; E2 region C 0.063-0.072 against 0.0137.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Rendering is cheaper with the table: 9x per-frame GPU and 3-6x edit-to-first-frame wall at matched quality 0.05 / 0.03.
worklog_interpretations.source: docs/worklogs/86 (Economics; Observation 6; verdict row END-TO-END ECONOMICS, NOT TESTED)
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Against one comparator only: a no-Russian-roulette 6-vertex Dr.Jit path tracer with the same ER, on undenoised whole-image relative L1 (noise-dominated; PT 133-745 spp vs ECRO 78-464 spp). The 9x is 5.45x lower kernel cost per sample times a 1.6-1.7x sample reduction. No physically computed table, explicit patch transport or optimised path tracer was timed; quality level g was not reached by either arm; region C on E2 has a bias floor near 0.073.

worklog_interpretations.claim: Geometry-state necessity is weakened: the state update matters only locally (A, the panel) and selective update has no cost benefit at this scale.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: STALE/ECRO E_H ratio 2.6-3.9x in A and 7-8x on E1's panel, 0.87-1.6x elsewhere; D change slope 0.46-0.65 with the stale state against 0.78-0.95; selective 21 ms vs full 26-28 ms wall.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The failing quantity is a static level error of a few whole Lambert patches (back wall left of centre, facing side of box B), exposed by the panel's near-mirror readout; the camera readout is an amplifier, not a defect.
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: Exact importance decomposition of the rendered signed error: level part -0.058 to -0.069 against directional part -0.002 to -0.004 (E2 T1 C); present at T0 (-0.058 / -0.055) and T1; back-wall field relative L1 0.044-0.045 against oracle half-noise 0.043 on E2 T1 only (E2 T0 0.048-0.050, E1 T1 0.063-0.065).

worklog_interpretations.claim: The source encoding is not what is missing in the failing cases: an incident field with the same encoding leaves the truth unchanged within noise (H_A falsified; source encoding WEAKENED).
worklog_interpretations.what_was_actually_measured: For ONE member of the equivalence class (bin-uniform direction, patch-uniform irradiance, re-emitted then transported exactly), region C's importance-weighted signed reading differs from the true light by 0.0001-0.002 (resolution about 0.006-0.009) in three configurations with one point light each; rendered E_H rises by 0.003-0.008. It shows that a linear, geometry-determined operator on s exists that reproduces these readings; it does not test other encoding-equivalent fields, patch-level placement beyond region C's weights, the operator's internal bin / patch / ray discretisation of intermediate radiance, or expressibility in the rank-16 / rank-24 factor form.

worklog_interpretations.claim: The 64-bin encoding does lose information for a narrow beam on the sharp panel (2.8x different region-C reading at identical encodings).
